    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The

    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()

def _run_shard(agent_timeout="", progress_extension=""):
    env = dict(os.environ)

def _tb_args(stdout):
    args = []
    inside = False
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line == "TB_BEGIN":
            inside = True
        elif line == "TB_END":
            inside = False
        elif inside and line.startswith("arg:"):

    return args


def _env_value(stdout, name):
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith(name + "="):

    return None

Harbor installs a SIGTERM handler (`signal.signal`) that raises KeyboardInterrupt — a sync signal handler. Important design consequence:

- `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` would REPLACE harbor's `signal.signal` handler (they conflict — asyncio's add_signal_handler uses signal.set_wakeup_fd + signal.signal internally; installing via the loop overrides the signal.signal handler). When our run ends we can restore harbor's by `signal.signal(SIGTERM, harbor's original)` — capture with `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` before overriding.

But there's a simpler, compatible design: instead of `loop.add_signal_handler`, install a PLAIN `signal.signal(SIGTERM, our_sync_handler)` (chaining to the previous handler). A sync handler runs in the main thread between bytecodes; it can set a flag and schedule the async flush via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. arguments.newText:
gh-1556 AC7: when any knob above arms an adapter-side cap, the adapters
also export FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = now + (effective cap - 120s wrap-up
margin) into the agent session, so fa's own deadline awareness can steer
wrap-up before the kill. With no knobs the export is absent — fa never
invents a clock (see deadline_epoch_ms / deadline_env_from).

Round 5 (gh-1576) — cap resolution: the deadline becomes TRUTHFUL when an
external harness caps the trial below fa's own knobs. The incident
(TB 2.1, run 38271607849): harbor hard-killed four extract-moves-from-video
trials at the dataset-declared 1800s while fa planned against the adapter's
3600s abs ceiling — the T-3min wrap-up steer was armed at minute 57 and
never fired, and the audit writer never ran because the kill came from
outside. The fix is a protocol, not a knob: the workflow resolves each
shard task's declared agent timeout (task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`)
BEFORE launch and exports it as

  FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC          external harness cap seconds (empty/absent
                               = unknown — knobs rule alone, byte-for-byte
                               today; malformed/<= 0/absurd values are
                               rejected with a warning, knobs-only fallback)

and every deadline computation composes effective_cap = min(external,
knob) with the winning source recorded in the audit. Invariant I1: fa
NEVER sees a deadline later than any known external cap. Invariant I2:
every trial termination leaves the audit (the adapters add incremental
checkpoints plus a SIGTERM/SIGINT and cancellation flush so an external
kill still lands a final record with outcome external_kill; the adapter's
own kill AT the external cap is outcome external_cap). The ProgressWatch /
ProgressLadder kill deadlines clamp to the external cap the same way, so
the adapter — not harbor's blind wait_for — decides and audits the kill
whenever it can. SIGKILL still leaves nothing in-container (non-goal);
the incremental checkpoints are the best-effort residue.

#!/bin/sh
# Builds the fa CLI bundle and runs it against terminal-bench.
#
# Usage:
#   ./run.sh -t hello-world                     # specific task ids / globs
#   TASKS="-t chess-best-move -t fix-git" ./run.sh
#   ./run.sh -t 'crack-7z-hash*'                # glob supported by tb
#
# Environment:
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / <apiKeyEnvVar> — fa provider
#   preconfig passed through to the container (see env_provider_preconfig).
#   DATASET (default terminal-bench-core==0.1.1), OUT (default /tmp/tb-runs).
#   TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER (default 2) — tb --global-timeout-multiplier; the
#   dataset's declared task timeouts (median 360s agent / 60s test) assume a
#   fast model and a warm container network. The 0.1.1 baseline run
#   (issue #142) lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
#   phases still apt-installing their own deps when the 60s cap hit.
#   TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR (default 120) — pads the dataset's declared
#   max_test_timeout_sec up to this floor before the run (gh-1206:
#   slow-start server tasks and judge phases installing their own deps
#   burn the 60s tb default and die as test_timeout with the agent DONE;
#   240s effective at multiplier 2; a cap is a cap, not a wait, so fast
#   verifier phases are unaffected). 0 = declared budgets unchanged.
#   On top of the floor, the gh-1407 per-task override table
#   (test_budget_overrides.json — runner-measured test-phase p95 per
#   repeat-offender task) pads those tasks so effective >= p95 x 1.5.
#
# tb needs the docker socket; run via sudo with the user env preserved:
#   sudo -n env HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH bench/terminal_bench/run.sh -t hello-world
set -e

REPO=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
DATASET=${DATASET:-terminal-bench-core==0.1.1}
case "$DATASET" in *==*) ;; *) echo "DATASET must be name==version, got: $DATASET" >&2; exit 1;; esac
OUT=${OUT:-/tmp/tb-runs}
TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER=${TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER:-2}
TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR=${TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR:-120}
BUNDLE=$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle

echo "==> building fa bundle"
(cd "$REPO" && dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$BUNDLE")

echo "==> packing bundle"
tar -czf /tmp/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$BUNDLE/bundle" .

echo "==> fetching dataset into tb cache (skipped when present)"
tb datasets download -d "$DATASET"
DS_CACHE="$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}"
python3 "$REPO/bench/terminal_bench/patch_dataset.py" "$DS_CACHE"
python3 "$REPO/bench/terminal_bench/patch_test_timeouts.py" "$DS_CACHE" \
    --floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR" --multiplier "$TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER"

echo "==> running terminal-bench"
export FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL=/tmp/fa-bundle.tar.gz
export PYTHONPATH="$REPO/bench/terminal_bench${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

# shellcheck disable=SC2086
exec tb run -d "$DATASET" --agent-import-path fa_agent:FaAgent \
    --output-path "$OUT" --no-cleanup --global-timeout-multiplier "$TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER" "$@"

Confirmed the pinned facts:
1. Harbor wraps `agent.run(...)` in `asyncio.wait_for(run(...), timeout=timeout_sec)` — the timeout comes from `task.config.agent.timeout_sec` (task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`), possibly overridden by `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` / max / multiplier. When it times out → CancelledError into our run() coroutine, then harbor raises AgentTimeoutError.
2. The per-task timeout is NOT passed into `BaseInstalledAgent.perform_task`/`run` — pinned negative fact confirmed.

Also important: `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` — the harbor run config can override. The workflow doesn't pass agent override timeouts (no `--agent-timeout` flag to harbor run in bench-harbor.yml — let me double check the harbor run invocation: `harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" --job-name ... -o jobs "${args[@]}"` where args are `-i <task>` pairs. No timeout overrides. So the effective external cap = task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`.

Now — is it visible whether CancelledError is delivered once? In harbor's `wait_for`, on timeout the inner task is cancelled and TimeoutError raised. Our `run()` coroutine gets CancelledError at its current await point (once). Our except CancelledError handler can await (the exception was already delivered). Python 3.12: asyncio.wait_for cancels the inner future/task and waits for it. So yes, one delivery. (Note: 3.12's wait_for uses timeouts module; still one cancel.)

One more check — the harbor `run` command line in the workflow doesn't pass `-t/--agent-timeout-multiplier`? Defaults 1.0. Good.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the knob/timeout shell logic of the bench.yml shard step (gh-1209).

The `run:` block decides, from two workflow_dispatch inputs, whether the
outer tb harness cap must sit above the progress ladder's ceiling and which
env vars reach fa_agent.py. This suite executes that exact block against a
`tb` stub and pins one behavior per input combination:

- REG-1 (issue #1122): both inputs absent → byte-for-byte stock delegation —
  no FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC, no FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION, no --global-agent-
  timeout-sec.
- gh-1209: any active ladder (explicit agent-timeout, or progress-extension
  on with its 360s default base) pins the harness cap at 4x base + 180s so
  the ladder decides, never the flat harness wait_for.
- gh-1209 review: `agent-timeout=0` is rejected at step start — it used to
  pass validation, export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=0, and raise ValueError
  inside EVERY trial's perform_task hours into the shard.
- Invalid inputs (non-digit timeout, non-boolean extension) fail fast.

Issue #1406: the fa launch path must carry the ConnTrace env into the
tmux pane itself (string-level asserts on the generated TerminalCommand
— the exact bytes tb types into the pane), and a trial whose
bench_metrics.json folded zero requests despite real model usage must
fire a LOUD workflow warning, never ship an empty shell silently.

gh-1471: the setup-job provider resolve step maps the dispatch choice
(zai-glm-5.3-flash default / kimi-for-coding / custom) to the full
provider triple and preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard
starts — each choice pins (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar), an
unmapped value fails hard, a missing secret fails fast naming the
secret, and a key value never reaches the log. The custom path (D1 /
AC 2a) validates the provider-config JSON (parseable object, non-empty
https:// baseUrl + model, no key-like fields case-insensitively at any
depth, plus the Dart preconfig contract mirror: closed key whitelist,
capability integer+floor pair, type/input/thinkingLevel shapes) and
injects the fixed apiKeyEnvVar FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM — the key comes only
from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY. REG-1: the default's provider_config is
byte-identical to the pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON.

def _shard_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the tb shard step from bench.yml.

    Text-slicing, not PyYAML: the block is a literal scalar and the suite
    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The
    block is identified by its `tb run -d` body, so unrelated `run:` blocks
    never match.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:

_TB_STUB = r"""

  echo "TB_BEGIN"
  local a
  for a in "$@"; do echo "arg:$a"; done
  echo "TB_END"
  echo "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC-__unset__}"
  echo "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=${FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION-__unset__}"
  echo "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC=${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC-__unset__}"
}
"""

_DRIVER = "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _TB_STUB + "\n" + _shard_run_block() + "\n"


def _run_shard(agent_timeout="", progress_extension=""):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(
        {
            "DATASET": "/tmp/fa-bench-workflow-test-dataset",
            "SHARD_TASKS": "task-0 task-1",
            "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI": "test-key",
            # gh-1471: the resolve step (setup job) names the key env var
            # for the run block's indirection; the zai default names the
            # zai var.
            "FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV": "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI",
            "AGENT_TIMEOUT": agent_timeout,
            "PROGRESS_EXTENSION": progress_extension,
        }
    )
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        driver = Path(tmp) / "shard_step.sh"
        driver.write_text(_DRIVER)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(driver)],
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
        )
    return proc


def _tb_args(stdout):
    args = []
    inside = False
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line == "TB_BEGIN":
            inside = True
        elif line == "TB_END":
            inside = False
        elif inside and line.startswith("arg:"):
            args.append(line[len("arg:") :])
    return args


def _env_value(stdout, name):
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith(name + "="):
            return line[len(name) + 1 :]
    return None


def _flag_value(args, flag):
    return args[args.index(flag) + 1] if flag in args else None

        self.assertEqual(_env_value(proc.stdout, "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION"), "__unset__")
        args = _tb_args(proc.stdout)

blocks.text:
Harbor installs a SIGTERM handler (`signal.signal`) that raises KeyboardInterrupt — a sync signal handler. Important design consequence:

- `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` would REPLACE harbor's `signal.signal` handler (they conflict — asyncio's add_signal_handler uses signal.set_wakeup_fd + signal.signal internally; installing via the loop overrides the signal.signal handler). When our run ends we can restore harbor's by `signal.signal(SIGTERM, harbor's original)` — capture with `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` before overriding.

But there's a simpler, compatible design: instead of `loop.add_signal_handler`, install a PLAIN `signal.signal(SIGTERM, our_sync_handler)` (chaining to the previous handler). A sync handler runs in the main thread between bytecodes; it can set a flag and schedule the async flush via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. But if the previous handler was harbor's `_handle_sigterm` (raise KeyboardInterrupt), what should OUR handler do? The chain: our handler runs → schedule flush → then call the previous behavior (raise KeyboardInterrupt) → harbor unwinds. The flush task gets scheduled on the loop; whether it runs before teardown depends... KeyboardInterrupt in the main thread interrupts the loop; the scheduled callback may still run if the loop handles it during unwinding — uncertain.

Honestly: the DOMINANT external-kill path (the incident) is harbor's wait_for → CancelledError — fully reliable in-adapter, and that's what IT-3's "external kill at the cap" exercises. The SIGTERM handler is for `docker stop`/orchestrator SIGTERM of the harbor process. I'll implement the SIGTERM/SIGINT handler as a plain sync handler that:
1. Captures previous handler; installs ours at run start (main thread only).
2. Ours: records the signal name on a shared state object, schedules the audit flush (via call_soon_threadsafe onto the running loop — flush is async exec into the container), then chains to the previous handler (preserving harbor's KeyboardInterrupt semantics / default termination).
3. Restores the previous handler in finally.

The flush races process teardown — best-effort by design (the checkpoint files are the durable layer). This is honest about the limits while satisfying IT-3's "handler writes final audit on signal" at the mechanism level (unit-testable by invoking the handler).

Now, let me also confirm: the incremental checkpoints must land somewhere that survives harbor kills. Container /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json — survives until container teardown (harbor tears down the env AFTER the trial finishes — including after wait_for timeout → our CancelledError flush + the sync'd checkpoints are downloaded with agent logs ✓). For SIGKILL of the harbor PROCESS, the container may stay (docker) with the checkpoint inside — post-mortem can still read it (E3 note).

OK — design is settled. One more decision: where does the tb adapter write checkpoints? Host-side `logging_dir/fa-agent-timeout.json` — partial writes (outcome "running", checkpoint: true) at each progress sample; final write overwrites. tb's harness SIGKILL leaves the checkpoint ✓.

        self.assertEqual(

            (1800.0, "known"),

        self.assertEqual(

content.text: Now add the cap-resolution core after the `_flag` helper:

arguments.newText:
def _flag(env, name, default=False):
    raw = _optional(env, name)
    if raw is None:
        return default
    value = raw.lower()
    if value in _FLAG_TRUE:
        return True
    if value in _FLAG_FALSE:
        return False
    # A mistyped flag must never silently disable the extension (a silent
    # mis-parse costs a multi-hour run) - fail loud, same as _number().
    raise ValueError(f"{name} must be boolean (true/false), got: {raw!r}")


# ── Cap resolution (gh-1576) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# The external harness cap (harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`, tb's
# harness cap) resolved by the workflow BEFORE launch and exported as
# FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC. Unlike the knob knobs (fail-loud: a mistyped knob
# costs a whole shard) a malformed cap DEGRADES: knobs-only fallback with
# a warning — the run must never crash inside a trial over harness
# metadata, and it must never arm a clock off garbage either.
EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"

# Anything above this is rejected as absurd rather than trusted: the
# exported deadline is now_ms + cap*1000 and must stay inside an int64
# (Dart int) with room to spare. Real harness caps are minutes-to-hours;
# 1e12 seconds (~31,700 years) is unreachably far above any of them.
_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC = 1e12

EXTERNAL_KNOWN = "known"
EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
EXTERNAL_REJECTED = "rejected"

# The verdict names for the audit's outcome field.
_EXTERNAL_CAP = "external_cap"
_ABS_CEILING = "abs_ceiling"  # noqa: F811 — kept next to its sibling verdicts


def external_cap_from_env(env=None, quiet: bool = False):
    """(cap_sec | None, status) for FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC — never raises.

    status: EXTERNAL_KNOWN (a finite, positive, sane number) |
    EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN (absent or blank — no cap was exported) |
    EXTERNAL_REJECTED (malformed / <= 0 / non-finite / absurdly large:
    ignored with a warning, knobs-only fallback — AC8). quiet=True
    suppresses the warning for callers that log it themselves.
    """
    raw = _optional(env if env is not None else os.environ, EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV)
    if raw is None:
        return None, EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0 or value > _EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    return value, EXTERNAL_KNOWN


def _reject(raw: str, quiet: bool):
    if not quiet:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV}={raw!r} is not a usable cap (need a finite "
            f"positive number of seconds <= {_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:g}); "
            "ignoring it — the effective cap falls back to the adapter "
            "knobs alone (gh-1576 AC8)",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=3,
        )
    return None, EXTERNAL_REJECTED


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapResolution:
    """The min() of every known cap input, with the winner recorded (I1).

    knob_cap_sec is None when no adapter knob is set (the adapter's own
    cap is unknown); external_cap_sec is None when the external cap is
    unknown or rejected (status says which). At least one input is known
    whenever a CapResolution exists — resolve_cap returns None when
    NOTHING is known, the byte-identical no-clock contract.
    """

    external_cap_status: str
    effective_cap_sec: float
    winning_cap_source: str
    knob_cap_sec: float | None = None
    external_cap_sec: float | None = None
    # E7: the wrap-up margin does not fit under the cap — the deadline
    # clamps instead of lying (or going negative). Recorded, not silent.
    deadline_clamped: bool = False

    def audit_fields(self, deadline_epoch_ms: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """The audit's cap_resolution block (AC2: source + both inputs)."""
        fields = {
            "external_cap_status": self.external_cap_status,
            "effective_cap_sec": self.effective_cap_sec,
            "winning_cap_source": self.winning_cap_source,
            "deadline_clamped": self.deadline_clamped,
        }
        if self.external_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["external_cap_sec"] = self.external_cap_sec
        if self.knob_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["knob_cap_sec"] = self.knob_cap_sec
        if deadline_epoch_ms is not None:
            fields["deadline_epoch_ms"] = deadline_epoch_ms
        return fields


def resolve_cap(
    knobs: "TimeoutKnobs | None",
    env=None,
    test_budget_sec: float = 0.0,
    quiet: bool = False,
) -> "CapResolution | None":
    """Compose every known cap input: effective = min(external, knobs).

    Returns None only when NO input is known — no knobs and no usable
    external cap — the pre-gh-1576 no-clock contract byte-for-byte
    (AC5/REG-2). The winning source is `external` on ties (E5): the
    harness is the stricter truth.
    """
    external, status = external_cap_from_env(env, quiet=quiet)
    knob_cap = (
        effective_cap_sec(knobs, test_budget_sec) if knobs is not None else None
    )
    if knob_cap is None and external is None:
        return None
    if external is None:
        effective, source = knob_cap, "knobs"
    elif knob_cap is None:
        effective, source = external, "external"
    else:
        effective = min(external, knob_cap)
        source = "external" if external <= knob_cap else "knobs"
    return CapResolution(
        external_cap_status=status,
        effective_cap_sec=effective,
        winning_cap_source=source,
        knob_cap_sec=knob_cap,
        external_cap_sec=external,
        # E7: the shipped wrap-up margin cannot fit under this cap — the
        # deadline will clamp to the cap itself (recorded in the audit).
        deadline_clamped=effective - _DEADLINE_MARGIN_SEC <= 0,
    )

blocks.text:
The task.toml format has:

```toml
[agent]
timeout_sec = 1800.0
```

So the cap discovery: read `[agent] timeout_sec` from each task dir's `task.toml`. The preference in the ticket's open question 1: "read the dataset task.toml per shard task in the workflow (simple, matches how SHARD_TASKS already resolves names)". The setup job downloads the dataset and runs split_tasks.py. I'll extend split_tasks.py to emit per-shard external caps: min of declared `[agent] timeout_sec` across each shard's tasks, emitted as `external_cap` in the matrix include entries (and a flat listing in non-shard mode). Then bench-harbor.yml maps `FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}` (empty when absent → treated as unknown).

Note `[verifier] timeout_sec = 1800` also exists — we read `[agent] timeout_sec` only.

Wait — actually, is the tb (terminal_bench legacy) harness cap also in the dataset? For terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 (legacy bench.yml path), the harness cap is configured differently. Open question 2 says default = wire FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC for tb adapter parity. The shared module handles the env; the tb adapter picks it up automatically via `deadline_env_from()`. Does bench.yml need to export FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC? bench.yml uses terminal-bench-core==0.1.1 whose task format doesn't have [agent] timeout_sec (old format: task.yaml). That legacy path can stay — the tb adapter honors FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC if a harness ever exports it. For parity wiring in the legacy tb workflow — bench.yml doesn't have dataset-declared caps in the old format; skip bench.yml plumbing, note it.

Now let me check the tb run.sh to see whether there's an external cap knob there.

Also — very important — how does harbor pass the per-task timeout? The adapter never sees it (pinned fact). Our workflow-level export resolves it pre-launch. Since a shard has multiple tasks, exporting the MIN of declared caps is the conservative truth (never above any known external cap — I1). And an operator-set `agent-timeout` input... that's FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC (a knob), already min'ed via knobs.

Now the plan for implementation:

### 1. `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py`

- Add `EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"` and parse in a new function:

```python
_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC = 1e12  # keeps now_ms + cap*1000 inside an int64

def external_cap_from_env(env=None) -> tuple[float | None, str]:
    """(cap, status): status in {"known", "unknown", "rejected"}."""
```
Validation: absent/blank → (None, "unknown"); non-numeric / <= 0 / non-finite / > max → (None, "rejected") + warnings.warn.

- `resolve_cap(knobs, env=None, test_budget_sec=0.0) -> CapResolution | None`:
  Returns None only when knobs is None AND external cap unknown/rejected (feature fully off — byte-identical no-knobs path). Otherwise a record:
  - knob_cap = effective_cap_sec(knobs) when knobs is not None else None (knobs absent)
  - external = parsed cap or None
  - effective = min of known inputs
  - winning source: "external" when external is not None and external <= knob_cap (tie → external, E5); else "knobs" (when knobs present); when knobs absent → "external".

#!/bin/sh
# Builds the fa CLI bundle and runs it against terminal-bench.
#
# Usage:
#   ./run.sh -t hello-world                     # specific task ids / globs
#   TASKS="-t chess-best-move -t fix-git" ./run.sh
#   ./run.sh -t 'crack-7z-hash*'                # glob supported by tb
#
# Environment:
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / <apiKeyEnvVar> — fa provider
#   preconfig passed through to the container (see env_provider_preconfig).
#   DATASET (default terminal-bench-core==0.1.1), OUT (default /tmp/tb-runs).
#   TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER (default 2) — tb --global-timeout-multiplier; the
#   dataset's declared task timeouts (median 360s agent / 60s test) assume a
#   fast model and a warm container network. The 0.1.1 baseline run
#   (issue #142) lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
#   phases still apt-installing their own deps when the 60s cap hit.
#   TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR (default 120) — pads the dataset's declared
#   max_test_timeout_sec up to this floor before the run (gh-1206:
#   slow-start server tasks and judge phases installing their own deps
#   burn the 60s tb default and die as test_timeout with the agent DONE;
#   240s effective at multiplier 2; a cap is a cap, not a wait, so fast
#   verifier phases are unaffected). 0 = declared budgets unchanged.
#   On top of the floor, the gh-1407 per-task override table
#   (test_budget_overrides.json — runner-measured test-phase p95 per
#   repeat-offender task) pads those tasks so effective >= p95 x 1.5.
#
# tb needs the docker socket; run via sudo with the user env preserved:
#   sudo -n env HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH bench/terminal_bench/run.sh -t hello-world
set -e

REPO=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
DATASET=${DATASET:-terminal-bench-core==0.1.1}
case "$DATASET" in *==*) ;; *) echo "DATASET must be name==version, got: $DATASET" >&2; exit 1;; esac
OUT=${OUT:-/tmp/tb-runs}
TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER=${TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER:-2}
TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR=${TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR:-120}
BUNDLE=$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle

echo "==> building fa bundle"
(cd "$REPO" && dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$BUNDLE")

echo "==> packing bundle"
tar -czf /tmp/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$BUNDLE/bundle" .

echo "==> fetching dataset into tb cache (skipped when present)"
tb datasets download -d "$DATASET"
DS_CACHE="$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}"
python3 "$REPO/bench/terminal_bench/patch_dataset.py" "$DS_CACHE"
python3 "$REPO/bench/terminal_bench/patch_test_timeouts.py" "$DS_CACHE" \
    --floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR" --multiplier "$TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER"

echo "==> running terminal-bench"
export FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL=/tmp/fa-bundle.tar.gz
export PYTHONPATH="$REPO/bench/terminal_bench${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

# shellcheck disable=SC2086
exec tb run -d "$DATASET" --agent-import-path fa_agent:FaAgent \
    --output-path "$OUT" --no-cleanup --global-timeout-multiplier "$TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER" "$@"

Harbor wraps `agent.run(...)` in `asyncio.wait_for(run(...), timeout=timeout_sec)` — the timeout comes from `task.config.agent.timeout_sec` (task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`), possibly overridden by `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` / max / multiplier. When it times out → CancelledError into our run() coroutine, then harbor raises AgentTimeoutError.
2. The per-task timeout is NOT passed into `BaseInstalledAgent.perform_task`/`run` — pinned negative fact confirmed.

Also important: `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` — the harbor run config can override. The workflow doesn't pass agent override timeouts (no `--agent-timeout` flag to harbor run in bench-harbor.yml — let me double check the harbor run invocation: `harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" --job-name ... -o jobs "${args[@]}"` where args are `-i <task>` pairs. No timeout overrides. So the effective external cap = task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`.

Now — is it visible whether CancelledError is delivered once? In harbor's `wait_for`, on timeout the inner task is cancelled and TimeoutError raised. Our `run()` coroutine gets CancelledError at its current await point (once). Our except CancelledError handler can await (the exception was already delivered). Python 3.12: asyncio.wait_for cancels the inner future/task and waits for it. So yes, one delivery. (Note: 3.12's wait_for uses timeouts module; still one cancel.)

Harbor installs a SIGTERM handler (`signal.signal`) that raises KeyboardInterrupt — a sync signal handler. Important design consequence:

- `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` would REPLACE harbor's `signal.signal` handler (they conflict — asyncio's add_signal_handler uses signal.set_wakeup_fd + signal.signal internally; installing via the loop overrides the signal.signal handler). When our run ends we can restore harbor's by `signal.signal(SIGTERM, harbor's original)` — capture with `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` before overriding.

But there's a simpler, compatible design: instead of `loop.add_signal_handler`, install a PLAIN `signal.signal(SIGTERM, our_sync_handler)` (chaining to the previous handler). A sync handler runs in the main thread between bytecodes; it can set a flag and schedule the async flush via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. But if the previous handler was harbor's `_handle_sigterm` (raise KeyboardInterrupt), what should OUR handler do? The chain: our handler runs → schedule flush → then call the previous behavior (raise KeyboardInterrupt) → harbor unwinds. The flush task gets scheduled on the loop; whether it runs before teardown depends... KeyboardInterrupt in the main thread interrupts the loop; the scheduled callback may still run if the loop handles it during unwinding — uncertain.

Honestly: the DOMINANT external-kill path (the incident) is harbor's wait_for → CancelledError — fully reliable in-adapter, and that's what IT-3's "external kill at the cap" exercises. The SIGTERM handler is for `docker stop`/orchestrator SIGTERM of the harbor process. I'll implement the SIGTERM/SIGINT handler as a plain sync handler that:
1. Captures previous handler; installs ours at run start (main thread only).
2. Ours: records the signal name on a shared state object, schedules the audit flush (via call_soon_threadsafe onto the running loop — flush is async exec into the container), then chains to the previous handler (preserving harbor's KeyboardInterrupt semantics / default termination).
3. Restores the previous handler in finally.

The flush races process teardown — best-effort by design (the checkpoint files are the durable layer). This is honest about the limits while satisfying IT-3's "handler writes final audit on signal" at the mechanism level (unit-testable by invoking the handler).

Now, let me also confirm: the incremental checkpoints must land somewhere that survives harbor kills. Container /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json — survives until container teardown (harbor tears down the env AFTER the trial finishes — including after wait_for timeout → our CancelledError flush + the sync'd checkpoints are downloaded with agent logs ✓). For SIGKILL of the harbor PROCESS, the container may stay (docker) with the checkpoint inside — post-mortem can still read it (E3 note).

# ── Cap resolution (gh-1576) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# The external harness cap (harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`, tb's
# harness cap) resolved by the workflow BEFORE launch and exported as
# FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC. Unlike the knob knobs (fail-loud: a mistyped knob
# costs a whole shard) a malformed cap DEGRADES: knobs-only fallback with
# a warning — the run must never crash inside a trial over harness
# metadata, and it must never arm a clock off garbage either.
EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"

# Anything above this is rejected as absurd rather than trusted: the
# exported deadline is now_ms + cap*1000 and must stay inside an int64
# (Dart int) with room to spare. Real harness caps are minutes-to-hours;
# 1e12 seconds (~31,700 years) is unreachably far above any of them.
_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC = 1e12

EXTERNAL_KNOWN = "known"
EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
EXTERNAL_REJECTED = "rejected"

# The verdict names for the audit's outcome field.
_EXTERNAL_CAP = "external_cap"
_ABS_CEILING = "abs_ceiling"  # noqa: F811 — kept next to its sibling verdicts


def external_cap_from_env(env=None, quiet: bool = False):
    """(cap_sec | None, status) for FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC — never raises.

    status: EXTERNAL_KNOWN (a finite, positive, sane number) |
    EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN (absent or blank — no cap was exported) |
    EXTERNAL_REJECTED (malformed / <= 0 / non-finite / absurdly large:
    ignored with a warning, knobs-only fallback — AC8). quiet=True
    suppresses the warning for callers that log it themselves.
    """
    raw = _optional(env if env is not None else os.environ, EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV)
    if raw is None:
        return None, EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0 or value > _EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    return value, EXTERNAL_KNOWN


def _reject(raw: str, quiet: bool):
    if not quiet:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV}={raw!r} is not a usable cap (need a finite "
            f"positive number of seconds <= {_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:g}); "
            "ignoring it — the effective cap falls back to the adapter "
            "knobs alone (gh-1576 AC8)",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=3,
        )
    return None, EXTERNAL_REJECTED


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapResolution:
    """The min() of every known cap input, with the winner recorded (I1).

    knob_cap_sec is None when no adapter knob is set (the adapter's own
    cap is unknown); external_cap_sec is None when the external cap is
    unknown or rejected (status says which). At least one input is known
    whenever a CapResolution exists — resolve_cap returns None when
    NOTHING is known, the byte-identical no-clock contract.
    """

    external_cap_status: str
    effective_cap_sec: float
    winning_cap_source: str
    knob_cap_sec: float | None = None
    external_cap_sec: float | None = None
    # E7: the wrap-up margin does not fit under the cap — the deadline
    # clamps instead of lying (or going negative). Recorded, not silent.
    deadline_clamped: bool = False

    def audit_fields(self, deadline_epoch_ms: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """The audit's cap_resolution block (AC2: source + both inputs)."""
        fields = {
            "external_cap_status": self.external_cap_status,
            "effective_cap_sec": self.effective_cap_sec,
            "winning_cap_source": self.winning_cap_source,
            "deadline_clamped": self.deadline_clamped,
        }
        if self.external_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["external_cap_sec"] = self.external_cap_sec
        if self.knob_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["knob_cap_sec"] = self.knob_cap_sec
        if deadline_epoch_ms is not None:
            fields["deadline_epoch_ms"] = deadline_epoch_ms
        return fields


def resolve_cap(
    knobs: "TimeoutKnobs | None",
    env=None,
    test_budget_sec: float = 0.0,
    quiet: bool = False,
) -> "CapResolution | None":
    """Compose every known cap input: effective = min(external, knobs).

    Returns None only when NO input is known — no knobs and no usable
    external cap — the pre-gh-1576 no-clock contract byte-for-byte

    harness is the stricter truth.

#!/bin/sh
# Builds the fa CLI bundle and runs it against terminal-bench.
#
# Usage:
#   ./run.sh -t hello-world                     # specific task ids / globs
#   TASKS="-t chess-best-move -t fix-git" ./run.sh
#   ./run.sh -t 'crack-7z-hash*'                # glob supported by tb
#
# Environment:
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / <apiKeyEnvVar> — fa provider
#   preconfig passed through to the container (see env_provider_preconfig).
#   DATASET (default terminal-bench-core==0.1.1), OUT (default /tmp/tb-runs).
#   TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER (default 2) — tb --global-timeout-multiplier; the
#   dataset's declared task timeouts (median 360s agent / 60s test) assume a
#   fast model and a warm container network. The 0.1.1 baseline run
#   (issue #142) lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
#   phases still apt-installing their own deps when the 60s cap hit.
#   TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR (default 120) — pads the dataset's declared
#   max_test_timeout_sec up to this floor before the run (gh-1206:
#   slow-start server tasks and judge phases installing their own deps
#   burn the 60s tb default and die as test_timeout with the agent DONE;
#   240s effective at multiplier 2; a cap is a cap, not a wait, so fast
#   verifier phases are unaffected). 0 = declared budgets unchanged.
#   On top of the floor, the gh-1407 per-task override table
#   (test_budget_overrides.json — runner-measured test-phase p95 per
#   repeat-offender task) pads those tasks so effective >= p95 x 1.5.
#
# tb needs the docker socket; run via sudo with the user env preserved:
#   sudo -n env HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH bench/terminal_bench/run.sh -t hello-world
set -e

REPO=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
DATASET=${DATASET:-terminal-bench-core==0.1.1}
case "$DATASET" in *==*) ;; *) echo "DATASET must be name==version, got: $DATASET" >&2; exit 1;; esac
OUT=${OUT:-/tmp/tb-runs}
TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER=${TIMEOUT_MULTIPLIER:-2}
TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR=${TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR:-120}
BUNDLE=$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle

echo "==> building fa bundle"
(cd "$REPO" && dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$BUNDLE")

echo "==> packing bundle"

Confirmed the pinned facts:
1. Harbor wraps `agent.run(...)` in `asyncio.wait_for(run(...), timeout=timeout_sec)` — the timeout comes from `task.config.agent.timeout_sec` (task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`), possibly overridden by `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` / max / multiplier. When it times out → CancelledError into our run() coroutine, then harbor raises AgentTimeoutError.
2. The per-task timeout is NOT passed into `BaseInstalledAgent.perform_task`/`run` — pinned negative fact confirmed.

Also important: `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` — the harbor run config can override. The workflow doesn't pass agent override timeouts (no `--agent-timeout` flag to harbor run in bench-harbor.yml — let me double check the harbor run invocation: `harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" --job-name ... -o jobs "${args[@]}"` where args are `-i <task>` pairs. No timeout overrides. So the effective external cap = task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`.

Now — is it visible whether CancelledError is delivered once? In harbor's `wait_for`, on timeout the inner task is cancelled and TimeoutError raised. Our `run()` coroutine gets CancelledError at its current await point (once). Our except CancelledError handler can await (the exception was already delivered). Python 3.12: asyncio.wait_for cancels the inner future/task and waits for it. So yes, one delivery. (Note: 3.12's wait_for uses timeouts module; still one cancel.)

One more check — the harbor `run` command line in the workflow doesn't pass `-t/--agent-timeout-multiplier`? Defaults 1.0. Good.

Harbor installs a SIGTERM handler (`signal.signal`) that raises KeyboardInterrupt — a sync signal handler. Important design consequence:

- `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` would REPLACE harbor's `signal.signal` handler (they conflict — asyncio's add_signal_handler uses signal.set_wakeup_fd + signal.signal internally; installing via the loop overrides the signal.signal handler). When our run ends we can restore harbor's by `signal.signal(SIGTERM, harbor's original)` — capture with `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` before overriding.

But there's a simpler, compatible design: instead of `loop.add_signal_handler`, install a PLAIN `signal.signal(SIGTERM, our_sync_handler)` (chaining to the previous handler). A sync handler runs in the main thread between bytecodes; it can set a flag and schedule the async flush via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. But if the previous handler was harbor's `_handle_sigterm` (raise KeyboardInterrupt), what should OUR handler do? The chain: our handler runs → schedule flush → then call the previous behavior (raise KeyboardInterrupt) → harbor unwinds. The flush task gets scheduled on the loop; whether it runs before teardown depends... KeyboardInterrupt in the main thread interrupts the loop; the scheduled callback may still run if the loop handles it during unwinding — uncertain.

Honestly: the DOMINANT external-kill path (the incident) is harbor's wait_for → CancelledError — fully reliable in-adapter, and that's what IT-3's "external kill at the cap" exercises. The SIGTERM handler is for `docker stop`/orchestrator SIGTERM of the harbor process. I'll implement the SIGTERM/SIGINT handler as a plain sync handler that:
1. Captures previous handler; installs ours at run start (main thread only).
2. Ours: records the signal name on a shared state object, schedules the audit flush (via call_soon_threadsafe onto the running loop — flush is async exec into the container), then chains to the previous handler (preserving harbor's KeyboardInterrupt semantics / default termination).
3. Restores the previous handler in finally.

        # AC5/E1: no cap exported (the workflow leaves the env var empty
        # when a shard's tasks declare no timeout) => unknown, not a zero.
        self.assertEqual(fa_agent_timeout.external_cap_from_env(clean_env_all()), (None, "unknown"))
        self.assertEqual(
            fa_agent_timeout.external_cap_from_env(clean_env_all(EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME="  ")),
            (None, "unknown"),
        )

    def test_integer_and_float_caps_are_known(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            fa_agent_timeout.external_cap_from_env(clean_env_all(EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME="1800")),
            (1800.0, "known"),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            fa_agent_timeout.external_cap_from_env(clean_env_all(EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME="1800.5")),
            (1800.5, "known"),

    def test_malformed_caps_are_rejected_with_a_warning(self):
        # AC8: non-numeric, <= 0, non-finite and absurdly large values are

{"newText":"def _flag(env, name, default=False):
    raw = _optional(env, name)
    if raw is None:
        return default
    value = raw.lower()

        return True

# ── Cap resolution (gh-1576) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# The external harness cap (harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`, tb's
# harness cap) resolved by the workflow BEFORE launch and exported as
# FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC. Unlike the knob knobs (fail-loud: a mistyped knob
# costs a whole shard) a malformed cap DEGRADES: knobs-only fallback with
# a warning — the run must never crash inside a trial over harness
# metadata, and it must never arm a clock off garbage either.
EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"

# Anything above this is rejected as absurd rather than trusted: the
# exported deadline is now_ms + cap*1000 and must stay inside an int64
# (Dart int) with room to spare. Real harness caps are minutes-to-hours;
# 1e12 seconds (~31,700 years) is unreachably far above any of them.
_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC = 1e12

EXTERNAL_KNOWN = "known"
EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
EXTERNAL_REJECTED = "rejected"

# The verdict names for the audit's outcome field.
_EXTERNAL_CAP = "external_cap"
_ABS_CEILING = "abs_ceiling"  # noqa: F811 — kept next to its sibling verdicts


def external_cap_from_env(env=None, quiet: bool = False):
    """(cap_sec | None, status) for FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC — never raises.

    status: EXTERNAL_KNOWN (a finite, positive, sane number) |
    EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN (absent or blank — no cap was exported) |
    EXTERNAL_REJECTED (malformed / <= 0 / non-finite / absurdly large:
    ignored with a warning, knobs-only fallback — AC8). quiet=True
    suppresses the warning for callers that log it themselves.
    """
    raw = _optional(env if env is not None else os.environ, EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV)
    if raw is None:
        return None, EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0 or value > _EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    return value, EXTERNAL_KNOWN


def _reject(raw: str, quiet: bool):
    if not quiet:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV}={raw!r} is not a usable cap (need a finite "
            f"positive number of seconds <= {_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:g}); "
            "ignoring it — the effective cap falls back to the adapter "
            "knobs alone (gh-1576 AC8)",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=3,
        )
    return None, EXTERNAL_REJECTED


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapResolution:
    """The min() of every known cap input, with the winner recorded (I1).

    knob_cap_sec is None when no adapter knob is set (the adapter's own
    cap is unknown); external_cap_sec is None when the external cap is
    unknown or rejected (status says which). At least one input is known
    whenever a CapResolution exists — resolve_cap returns None when
    NOTHING is known, the byte-identical no-clock contract.
    """

    external_cap_status: str
    effective_cap_sec: float
    winning_cap_source: str
    knob_cap_sec: float | None = None
    external_cap_sec: float | None = None
    # E7: the wrap-up margin does not fit under the cap — the deadline
    # clamps instead of lying (or going negative). Recorded, not silent.
    deadline_clamped: bool = False

    def audit_fields(self, deadline_epoch_ms: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """The audit's cap_resolution block (AC2: source + both inputs)."""
        fields = {
            "external_cap_status": self.external_cap_status,
            "effective_cap_sec": self.effective_cap_sec,
            "winning_cap_source": self.winning_cap_source,
            "deadline_clamped": self.deadline_clamped,
        }
        if self.external_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["external_cap_sec"] = self.external_cap_sec
        if self.knob_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["knob_cap_sec"] = self.knob_cap_sec
        if deadline_epoch_ms is not None:
            fields["deadline_epoch_ms"] = deadline_epoch_ms
        return fields


def resolve_cap(
    knobs: "TimeoutKnobs | None",
    env=None,
    test_budget_sec: float = 0.0,
    quiet: bool = False,
) -> "CapResolution | None":
    """Compose every known cap input: effective = min(external, knobs).

    Returns None only when NO input is known — no knobs and no usable
    external cap — the pre-gh-1576 no-clock contract byte-for-byte
    (AC5/REG-2). The winning source is `external` on ties (E5): the
    harness is the stricter truth.
    """
    external, status = external_cap_from_env(env, quiet=quiet)
    knob_cap = (
        effective_cap_sec(knobs, test_budget_sec) if knobs is not None else None
    )
    if knob_cap is None and external is None:
        return None
    if external is None:
        effective, source = knob_cap, "knobs"
    elif knob_cap is None:
        effective, source = external, "external"
    else:
        effective = min(external, knob_cap)
        source = "external" if external <= knob_cap else "knobs"
    return CapResolution(
        external_cap_status=status,
        effective_cap_sec=effective,
        winning_cap_source=source,
        knob_cap_sec=knob_cap,
        external_cap_sec=external,
        # E7: the shipped wrap-up margin cannot fit under this cap — the
        # deadline will clamp to the cap itself (recorded in the audit).
        deadline_clamped=effective - _DEADLINE_MARGIN_SEC <= 0,

Confirmed the pinned facts:
1. Harbor wraps `agent.run(...)` in `asyncio.wait_for(run(...), timeout=timeout_sec)` — the timeout comes from `task.config.agent.timeout_sec` (task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`), possibly overridden by `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` / max / multiplier. When it times out → CancelledError into our run() coroutine, then harbor raises AgentTimeoutError.
2. The per-task timeout is NOT passed into `BaseInstalledAgent.perform_task`/`run` — pinned negative fact confirmed.

Also important: `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` — the harbor run config can override. The workflow doesn't pass agent override timeouts (no `--agent-timeout` flag to harbor run in bench-harbor.yml — let me double check the harbor run invocation: `harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" --job-name ... -o jobs "${args[@]}"` where args are `-i <task>` pairs. No timeout overrides. So the effective external cap = task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`.

Now — is it visible whether CancelledError is delivered once? In harbor's `wait_for`, on timeout the inner task is cancelled and TimeoutError raised. Our `run()` coroutine gets CancelledError at its current await point (once). Our except CancelledError handler can await (the exception was already delivered). Python 3.12: asyncio.wait_for cancels the inner future/task and waits for it. So yes, one delivery. (Note: 3.12's wait_for uses timeouts module; still one cancel.)

One more check — the harbor `run` command line in the workflow doesn't pass `-t/--agent-timeout-multiplier`? Defaults 1.0. Good.

Now the tb (terminal-bench 0.2.18) side: does tb wrap the agent in wait_for? Let me check AbstractInstalledAgent and the tb runner for its external kill mechanics, since IT-3 for tb adapter... The ticket's IT-3 is adapter-generic. For tb, our adapter takes over the deadline when knobs set. The tb harness cap is `--global-agent-timeout-sec` (bench.yml). I'll wire parity there.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the knob/timeout shell logic of the bench.yml shard step (gh-1209).

The `run:` block decides, from two workflow_dispatch inputs, whether the
outer tb harness cap must sit above the progress ladder's ceiling and which
env vars reach fa_agent.py. This suite executes that exact block against a
`tb` stub and pins one behavior per input combination:

- REG-1 (issue #1122): both inputs absent → byte-for-byte stock delegation —
  no FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC, no FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION, no --global-agent-
  timeout-sec.
- gh-1209: any active ladder (explicit agent-timeout, or progress-extension
  on with its 360s default base) pins the harness cap at 4x base + 180s so
  the ladder decides, never the flat harness wait_for.
- gh-1209 review: `agent-timeout=0` is rejected at step start — it used to
  pass validation, export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=0, and raise ValueError
  inside EVERY trial's perform_task hours into the shard.
- Invalid inputs (non-digit timeout, non-boolean extension) fail fast.

Issue #1406: the fa launch path must carry the ConnTrace env into the
tmux pane itself (string-level asserts on the generated TerminalCommand
— the exact bytes tb types into the pane), and a trial whose
bench_metrics.json folded zero requests despite real model usage must
fire a LOUD workflow warning, never ship an empty shell silently.

gh-1471: the setup-job provider resolve step maps the dispatch choice
(zai-glm-5.3-flash default / kimi-for-coding / custom) to the full
provider triple and preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard
starts — each choice pins (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar), an
unmapped value fails hard, a missing secret fails fast naming the
secret, and a key value never reaches the log. The custom path (D1 /
AC 2a) validates the provider-config JSON (parseable object, non-empty
https:// baseUrl + model, no key-like fields case-insensitively at any
depth, plus the Dart preconfig contract mirror: closed key whitelist,
capability integer+floor pair, type/input/thinkingLevel shapes) and
injects the fixed apiKeyEnvVar FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM — the key comes only
from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY. REG-1: the default's provider_config is
byte-identical to the pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench

def _shard_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the tb shard step from bench.yml.

    Text-slicing, not PyYAML: the block is a literal scalar and the suite
    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The
    block is identified by its `tb run -d` body, so unrelated `run:` blocks
    never match.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "tb run -d" in block:
            start = True
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("tb shard step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    # Only expression the block may interpolate; anything else means the
    # workflow grew a new one and this harness needs the mapping extended.
    block = re.sub(r"\$\{\{\s*matrix\.i\s*\}\}", "0", block)
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in run block: {leftover}"
    return block

_DRIVER = "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _TB_STUB + "\n" + _shard_run_block() + "\n"


def _run_shard(agent_timeout="", progress_extension=""):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(
        {
            "DATASET": "/tmp/fa-bench-workflow-test-dataset",
            "SHARD_TASKS": "task-0 task-1",
            "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI": "test-key",
            # gh-1471: the resolve step (setup job) names the key env var
            # for the run block's indirection; the zai default names the
            # zai var.
            "FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV": "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI",
            "AGENT_TIMEOUT": agent_timeout,
            "PROGRESS_EXTENSION": progress_extension,
        }
    )
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        driver = Path(tmp) / "shard_step.sh"
        driver.write_text(_DRIVER)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(driver)],
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
        )
    return proc


def _tb_args(stdout):
    args = []
    inside = False
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line == "TB_BEGIN":
            inside = True
        elif line == "TB_END":
            inside = False
        elif inside and line.startswith("arg:"):
            args.append(line[len("arg:") :])
    return args


def _env_value(stdout, name):
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith(name + "="):
            return line[len(name) + 1 :]
    return None


def _flag_value(args, flag):
    return args[args.index(flag) + 1] if flag in args else None

Harbor installs a SIGTERM handler (`signal.signal`) that raises KeyboardInterrupt — a sync signal handler. Important design consequence:

- `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` would REPLACE harbor's `signal.signal` handler (they conflict — asyncio's add_signal_handler uses signal.set_wakeup_fd + signal.signal internally; installing via the loop overrides the signal.signal handler). When our run ends we can restore harbor's by `signal.signal(SIGTERM, harbor's original)` — capture with `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` before overriding.

But there's a simpler, compatible design: instead of `loop.add_signal_handler`, install a PLAIN `signal.signal(SIGTERM, our_sync_handler)` (chaining to the previous handler). A sync handler runs in the main thread between bytecodes; it can set a flag and schedule the async flush via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. But if the previous handler was harbor's `_handle_sigterm` (raise KeyboardInterrupt), what should OUR handler do? The chain: our handler runs → schedule flush → then call the previous behavior (raise KeyboardInterrupt) → harbor unwinds. The flush task gets scheduled on the loop; whether it runs before teardown depends... KeyboardInterrupt in the main thread interrupts the loop; the scheduled callback may still run if the loop handles it during unwinding — uncertain.

Honestly: the DOMINANT external-kill path (the incident) is harbor's wait_for → CancelledError — fully reliable in-adapter, and that's what IT-3's "external kill at the cap" exercises. The SIGTERM handler is for `docker stop`/orchestrator SIGTERM of the harbor process. I'll implement the SIGTERM/SIGINT handler as a plain sync handler that:
1. Captures previous handler; installs ours at run start (main thread only).
2. Ours: records the signal name on a shared state object, schedules the audit flush (via call_soon_threadsafe onto the running loop — flush is async exec into the container), then chains to the previous handler (preserving harbor's KeyboardInterrupt semantics / default termination).
3. Restores the previous handler in finally.

The flush races process teardown — best-effort by design (the checkpoint files are the durable layer). This is honest about the limits while satisfying IT-3's "handler writes final audit on signal" at the mechanism level (unit-testable by invoking the handler).

Now, let me also confirm: the incremental checkpoints must land somewhere that survives harbor kills. Container /logs/agent/fa-timeout-metadata.json — survives until container teardown (harbor tears down the env AFTER the trial finishes — including after wait_for timeout → our CancelledError flush + the sync'd checkpoints are downloaded with agent logs ✓). For SIGKILL of the harbor PROCESS, the container may stay (docker) with the checkpoint inside — post-mortem can still read it (E3 note).

{"newText":"def _flag(env, name, default=False):

# ── Cap resolution (gh-1576) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# The external harness cap (harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`, tb's
# harness cap) resolved by the workflow BEFORE launch and exported as
# FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC. Unlike the knob knobs (fail-loud: a mistyped knob
# costs a whole shard) a malformed cap DEGRADES: knobs-only fallback with
# a warning — the run must never crash inside a trial over harness
# metadata, and it must never arm a clock off garbage either.
EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"

# Anything above this is rejected as absurd rather than trusted: the
# exported deadline is now_ms + cap*1000 and must stay inside an int64
# (Dart int) with room to spare. Real harness caps are minutes-to-hours;
# 1e12 seconds (~31,700 years) is unreachably far above any of them.
_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC = 1e12

EXTERNAL_KNOWN = "known"
EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
EXTERNAL_REJECTED = "rejected"

# The verdict names for the audit's outcome field.
_EXTERNAL_CAP = "external_cap"
_ABS_CEILING = "abs_ceiling"  # noqa: F811 — kept next to its sibling verdicts


def external_cap_from_env(env=None, quiet: bool = False):
    """(cap_sec | None, status) for FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC — never raises.

    status: EXTERNAL_KNOWN (a finite, positive, sane number) |
    EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN (absent or blank — no cap was exported) |
    EXTERNAL_REJECTED (malformed / <= 0 / non-finite / absurdly large:
    ignored with a warning, knobs-only fallback — AC8). quiet=True
    suppresses the warning for callers that log it themselves.
    """
    raw = _optional(env if env is not None else os.environ, EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV)
    if raw is None:
        return None, EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0 or value > _EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    return value, EXTERNAL_KNOWN


def _reject(raw: str, quiet: bool):
    if not quiet:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV}={raw!r} is not a usable cap (need a finite "
            f"positive number of seconds <= {_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:g}); "
            "ignoring it — the effective cap falls back to the adapter "
            "knobs alone (gh-1576 AC8)",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=3,
        )
    return None, EXTERNAL_REJECTED

class CapResolution:
    """The min() of every known cap input, with the winner recorded (I1).

    knob_cap_sec is None when no adapter knob is set (the adapter's own
    cap is unknown); external_cap_sec is None when the external cap is
    unknown or rejected (status says which). At least one input is known
    whenever a CapResolution exists — resolve_cap returns None when
    NOTHING is known, the byte-identical no-clock contract.
    """

    external_cap_status: str
    effective_cap_sec: float
    winning_cap_source: str
    knob_cap_sec: float | None = None
    external_cap_sec: float | None = None
    # E7: the wrap-up margin does not fit under the cap — the deadline
    # clamps instead of lying (or going negative). Recorded, not silent.
    deadline_clamped: bool = False

    def audit_fields(self, deadline_epoch_ms: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """The audit's cap_resolution block (AC2: source + both inputs)."""

Confirmed the pinned facts:

Harbor wraps `agent.run(...)` in `asyncio.wait_for(run(...), timeout=timeout_sec)` — the timeout comes from `task.config.agent.timeout_sec` (task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`), possibly overridden by `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` / max / multiplier. When it times out → CancelledError into our run() coroutine, then harbor raises AgentTimeoutError.
2. The per-task timeout is NOT passed into `BaseInstalledAgent.perform_task`/`run` — pinned negative fact confirmed.

Also important: `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` — the harbor run config can override. The workflow doesn't pass agent override timeouts (no `--agent-timeout` flag to harbor run in bench-harbor.yml — let me double check the harbor run invocation: `harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" --job-name ... -o jobs "${args[@]}"` where args are `-i <task>` pairs. No timeout overrides. So the effective external cap = task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`.

Now — is it visible whether CancelledError is delivered once? In harbor's `wait_for`, on timeout the inner task is cancelled and TimeoutError raised. Our `run()` coroutine gets CancelledError at its current await point (once). Our except CancelledError handler can await (the exception was already delivered). Python 3.12: asyncio.wait_for cancels the inner future/task and waits for it. So yes, one delivery. (Note: 3.12's wait_for uses timeouts module; still one cancel.)

One more check — the harbor `run` command line in the workflow doesn't pass `-t/--agent-timeout-multiplier`? Defaults 1.0. Good.

blocks.text:
Harbor installs a SIGTERM handler (`signal.signal`) that raises KeyboardInterrupt — a sync signal handler. Important design consequence:

- `loop.add_signal_handler(SIGTERM, ...)` would REPLACE harbor's `signal.signal` handler (they conflict — asyncio's add_signal_handler uses signal.set_wakeup_fd + signal.signal internally; installing via the loop overrides the signal.signal handler). When our run ends we can restore harbor's by `signal.signal(SIGTERM, harbor's original)` — capture with `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` before overriding.

But there's a simpler, compatible design: instead of `loop.add_signal_handler`, install a PLAIN `signal.signal(SIGTERM, our_sync_handler)` (chaining to the previous handler). A sync handler runs in the main thread between bytecodes; it can set a flag and schedule the async flush via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`. But if the previous handler was harbor's `_handle_sigterm` (raise KeyboardInterrupt), what should OUR handler do? The chain: our handler runs → schedule flush → then call the previous behavior (raise KeyboardInterrupt) → harbor unwinds. The flush task gets scheduled on the loop; whether it runs before teardown depends... KeyboardInterrupt in the main thread interrupts the loop; the scheduled callback may still run if the loop handles it during unwinding — uncertain.

Honestly: the DOMINANT external-kill path (the incident) is harbor's wait_for → CancelledError — fully reliable in-adapter, and that's what IT-3's "external kill at the cap" exercises. The SIGTERM handler is for `docker stop`/orchestrator SIGTERM of the harbor process. I'll implement the SIGTERM/SIGINT handler as a plain sync handler that:
1. Captures previous handler; installs ours at run start (main thread only).

# ── Cap resolution (gh-1576) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# The external harness cap (harbor's per-task `[agent] timeout_sec`, tb's
# harness cap) resolved by the workflow BEFORE launch and exported as
# FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC. Unlike the knob knobs (fail-loud: a mistyped knob
# costs a whole shard) a malformed cap DEGRADES: knobs-only fallback with
# a warning — the run must never crash inside a trial over harness
# metadata, and it must never arm a clock off garbage either.
EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"

# Anything above this is rejected as absurd rather than trusted: the
# exported deadline is now_ms + cap*1000 and must stay inside an int64
# (Dart int) with room to spare. Real harness caps are minutes-to-hours;
# 1e12 seconds (~31,700 years) is unreachably far above any of them.
_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC = 1e12

EXTERNAL_KNOWN = "known"
EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
EXTERNAL_REJECTED = "rejected"

# The verdict names for the audit's outcome field.
_EXTERNAL_CAP = "external_cap"
_ABS_CEILING = "abs_ceiling"  # noqa: F811 — kept next to its sibling verdicts


def external_cap_from_env(env=None, quiet: bool = False):
    """(cap_sec | None, status) for FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC — never raises.

    status: EXTERNAL_KNOWN (a finite, positive, sane number) |
    EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN (absent or blank — no cap was exported) |
    EXTERNAL_REJECTED (malformed / <= 0 / non-finite / absurdly large:
    ignored with a warning, knobs-only fallback — AC8). quiet=True
    suppresses the warning for callers that log it themselves.
    """
    raw = _optional(env if env is not None else os.environ, EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV)
    if raw is None:
        return None, EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0 or value > _EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:
        return _reject(raw, quiet)
    return value, EXTERNAL_KNOWN


def _reject(raw: str, quiet: bool):
    if not quiet:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV}={raw!r} is not a usable cap (need a finite "
            f"positive number of seconds <= {_EXTERNAL_CAP_MAX_SEC:g}); "
            "ignoring it — the effective cap falls back to the adapter "
            "knobs alone (gh-1576 AC8)",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=3,
        )
    return None, EXTERNAL_REJECTED


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapResolution:
    """The min() of every known cap input, with the winner recorded (I1).

    knob_cap_sec is None when no adapter knob is set (the adapter's own
    cap is unknown); external_cap_sec is None when the external cap is
    unknown or rejected (status says which). At least one input is known
    whenever a CapResolution exists — resolve_cap returns None when
    NOTHING is known, the byte-identical no-clock contract.
    """

    external_cap_status: str
    effective_cap_sec: float
    winning_cap_source: str
    knob_cap_sec: float | None = None
    external_cap_sec: float | None = None
    # E7: the wrap-up margin does not fit under the cap — the deadline
    # clamps instead of lying (or going negative). Recorded, not silent.
    deadline_clamped: bool = False

    def audit_fields(self, deadline_epoch_ms: int | None = None) -> dict:
        """The audit's cap_resolution block (AC2: source + both inputs)."""
        fields = {
            "external_cap_status": self.external_cap_status,
            "effective_cap_sec": self.effective_cap_sec,
            "winning_cap_source": self.winning_cap_source,
            "deadline_clamped": self.deadline_clamped,
        }
        if self.external_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["external_cap_sec"] = self.external_cap_sec
        if self.knob_cap_sec is not None:
            fields["knob_cap_sec"] = self.knob_cap_sec
        if deadline_epoch_ms is not None:
            fields["deadline_epoch_ms"] = deadline_epoch_ms
        return fields


def resolve_cap(
    knobs: "TimeoutKnobs | None",
    env=None,
    test_budget_sec: float = 0.0,
    quiet: bool = False,
) -> "CapResolution | None":
    """Compose every known cap input: effective = min(external, knobs).

    Returns None only when NO input is known — no knobs and no usable
    external cap — the pre-gh-1576 no-clock contract byte-for-byte
    (AC5/REG-2). The winning source is `external` on ties (E5): the
    harness is the stricter truth.
    """
    external, status = external_cap_from_env(env, quiet=quiet)
    knob_cap = (
        effective_cap_sec(knobs, test_budget_sec) if knobs is not None else None
    )
    if knob_cap is None and external is None:
        return None
    if external is None:
        effective, source = knob_cap, "knobs"
    elif knob_cap is None:
        effective, source = external, "external"
    else:
        effective = min(external, knob_cap)
        source = "external" if external <= knob_cap else "knobs"
    return CapResolution(
        external_cap_status=status,
        effective_cap_sec=effective,
        winning_cap_source=source,
        knob_cap_sec=knob_cap,
        external_cap_sec=external,
        # E7: the shipped wrap-up margin cannot fit under this cap — the
        # deadline will clamp to the cap itself (recorded in the audit).

Confirmed the pinned facts:
1. Harbor wraps `agent.run(...)` in `asyncio.wait_for(run(...), timeout=timeout_sec)` — the timeout comes from `task.config.agent.timeout_sec` (task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`), possibly overridden by `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` / max / multiplier. When it times out → CancelledError into our run() coroutine, then harbor raises AgentTimeoutError.
2. The per-task timeout is NOT passed into `BaseInstalledAgent.perform_task`/`run` — pinned negative fact confirmed.

Also important: `config.agent.override_timeout_sec` — the harbor run config can override. The workflow doesn't pass agent override timeouts (no `--agent-timeout` flag to harbor run in bench-harbor.yml — let me double check the harbor run invocation: `harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" --job-name ... -o jobs "${args[@]}"` where args are `-i <task>` pairs. No timeout overrides. So the effective external cap = task.toml `[agent] timeout_sec`.

Now — is it visible whether CancelledError is delivered once? In harbor's `wait_for`, on timeout the inner task is cancelled and TimeoutError raised. Our `run()` coroutine gets CancelledError at its current await point (once). Our except CancelledError handler can await (the exception was already delivered). Python 3.12: asyncio.wait_for cancels the inner future/task and waits for it. So yes, one delivery. (Note: 3.12's wait_for uses timeouts module; still one cancel.)

One more check — the harbor `run` command line in the workflow doesn't pass `-t/--agent-timeout-multiplier`? Defaults 1.0. Good.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the knob/timeout shell logic of the bench.yml shard step (gh-1209).

The `run:` block decides, from two workflow_dispatch inputs, whether the
outer tb harness cap must sit above the progress ladder's ceiling and which
env vars reach fa_agent.py. This suite executes that exact block against a
`tb` stub and pins one behavior per input combination:

- REG-1 (issue #1122): both inputs absent → byte-for-byte stock delegation —
  no FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC, no FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION, no --global-agent-
  timeout-sec.
- gh-1209: any active ladder (explicit agent-timeout, or progress-extension
  on with its 360s default base) pins the harness cap at 4x base + 180s so
  the ladder decides, never the flat harness wait_for.
- gh-1209 review: `agent-timeout=0` is rejected at step start — it used to
  pass validation, export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=0, and raise ValueError
  inside EVERY trial's perform_task hours into the shard.
- Invalid inputs (non-digit timeout, non-boolean extension) fail fast.

Issue #1406: the fa launch path must carry the ConnTrace env into the
tmux pane itself (string-level asserts on the generated TerminalCommand
— the exact bytes tb types into the pane), and a trial whose
bench_metrics.json folded zero requests despite real model usage must
fire a LOUD workflow warning, never ship an empty shell silently.

gh-1471: the setup-job provider resolve step maps the dispatch choice
(zai-glm-5.3-flash default / kimi-for-coding / custom) to the full
provider triple and preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard
starts — each choice pins (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar), an
unmapped value fails hard, a missing secret fails fast naming the
secret, and a key value never reaches the log. The custom path (D1 /
AC 2a) validates the provider-config JSON (parseable object, non-empty
https:// baseUrl + model, no key-like fields case-insensitively at any
depth, plus the Dart preconfig contract mirror: closed key whitelist,
capability integer+floor pair, type/input/thinkingLevel shapes) and
injects the fixed apiKeyEnvVar FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM — the key comes only
from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY. REG-1: the default's provider_config is
byte-identical to the pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON.

def _shard_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the tb shard step from bench.yml.

    Text-slicing, not PyYAML: the block is a literal scalar and the suite
    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The
    block is identified by its `tb run -d` body, so unrelated `run:` blocks
    never match.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)

_TB_STUB = r"""

  echo "TB_BEGIN"
  local a
  for a in "$@"; do echo "arg:$a"; done
  echo "TB_END"
  echo "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC-__unset__}"
  echo "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=${FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION-__unset__}"
  echo "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC=${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC-__unset__}"
}
"""

_DRIVER = "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _TB_STUB + "\n" + _shard_run_block() + "\n"


def _run_shard(agent_timeout="", progress_extension=""):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(
        {
            "DATASET": "/tmp/fa-bench-workflow-test-dataset",
            "SHARD_TASKS": "task-0 task-1",
            "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI": "test-key",
            # gh-1471: the resolve step (setup job) names the key env var
            # for the run block's indirection; the zai default names the
            # zai var.
            "FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV": "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI",
            "AGENT_TIMEOUT": agent_timeout,
            "PROGRESS_EXTENSION": progress_extension,
        }
    )
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        driver = Path(tmp) / "shard_step.sh"
        driver.write_text(_DRIVER)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(driver)],
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
        )
    return proc


def _tb_args(stdout):
    args = []
    inside = False
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line == "TB_BEGIN":
            inside = True
        elif line == "TB_END":
            inside = False
        elif inside and line.startswith("arg:"):
            args.append(line[len("arg:") :])
    return args


def _env_value(stdout, name):
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith(name + "="):
            return line[len(name) + 1 :]
    return None


def _flag_value(args, flag):
    return args[args.index(flag) + 1] if flag in args else None

        self.assertEqual(_env_value(proc.stdout, "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION"), "__unset__")

        self.assertEqual(_env_value(proc.stdout, "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION"), "__unset__")
        args = _tb_args(proc.stdout)

        args = _tb_args(proc.stdout)

        self.assertEqual(_env_value(proc.stdout, "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION"), "__unset__")
