{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                        loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
                    )
                    await self._maybe_checkpoint(environment, knobs, ladder)
                    if outcome:
                        # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                        # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                        # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                        # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed
                        # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                        # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                        # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:
                        # a SOLVED task scored 0). The bracket trick matches the
                        # agent process but not this command line, and any kill
                        # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                        # bounds the trial.
                        try:
                            await self.exec_as_root(
                                environment,
                                command="pkill -f '[f]a --session-root' || true",
                                timeout_sec=15,
                            )
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        try:
                            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=60)
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        if not exec_task.done():
                            exec_task.cancel()
                            # An abandoned cancelled task is GC-destroyed with
                            # "pending task" warnings and its exception never
                            # retrieved - await the cancellation instead. Only our
                            # own cancellation is swallowed; an external cancel of
                            # this coroutine still propagates.
                            try:
                                await exec_task
                            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                                if not exec_task.cancelled():
                                    raise
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        break
            # Natural completion: awaiting the task surfaces the exec's own
            # failure (e.g. NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) - today's semantics
            # verbatim. The audit records the true outcome class: a crash must
            # not be labelled "completed" (issue #1122 round 1).
            error = None
            if not outcome:
                try:
                    await exec_task
                except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised below
                    error = exc
            await self._write_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder,
                outcome or ("crashed" if error is not None else "completed"),
                deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
                cap=cap,
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # gh-1576 (I2): harbor's wait_for fired first — the incident's
            # exact kill class (run 38271607849: four trials killed at
            # 1800.000s, zero audit files). The container is still up
            # during teardown, so the flush lands. Never masked by an exec
            # failure; the cancellation always re-raises.
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        if outcome:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(
                f"fa agent killed by bench timeout ladder: {outcome}"
            )
        if error is not None:
            raise error

    async def _run_external_cap_only(self, instruction: str, environment) -> None:
        """Unsupervised exec under a known external cap (gh-1576).

        The harness owns the kill; the adapter's whole job here is I1+I2:
        fa sees the truthful deadline (via _provider_env) and every
        termination — clean exit, external cancellation, SIGTERM — leaves
        the audit record.
        """
        cap = self._cap
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                await self.exec_as_agent(
                    environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                    env=self._provider_env,
                )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, None, None, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        await self._write_audit(
            environment, None, None, "completed",
            deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )

{"newText":"    async def _write_audit(
        self, environment, knobs, ladder, outcome, deadline_epoch_ms=None,
        cap=None, checkpoint=False, external_kill=None,
    ) -> None:
        # AC4 (issue #1122): audit trail synced back with the agent logs.
        # AC6 (issue #1185): the audit also documents the harness-originated
        # share of the progress sample — the ⏳ liveness lines the pane
        # counter counts as progress. Both numbers are byte measures taken
        # where the file lives (one exec, no stream round-trip: a 600s+
        # trial can leave tens of MB of pane bytes, and a transport decode
        # would make len(utf-8) disagree with the ladder's live wc -c).
        # Fields drop when the stream is unreadable, never fabricated.
        # gh-1576: cap carries the cap-resolution block (winning source +
        # both inputs); checkpoint rows skip the stream measurement (they
        # are partial markers, written on the poll loop) and an
        # external_kill flush records which signal/cause ended the trial.
        if checkpoint:
            progress = liveness = None
        else:
            progress, liveness = await self._measure_streams(environment)
        record = _timeout.audit_dict(
            knobs,
            ladder if knobs is not None else None,
            outcome,
            progress_bytes=progress,
            liveness_bytes=liveness,
            deadline_epoch_ms=deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )
        if checkpoint:
            record["checkpoint"] = True
        if external_kill:
            record["external_kill"] = external_kill
        payload = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(record).encode()).decode()
        try:
            await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    f"mkdir -p /logs/agent && printf %s {payload} "
                    f"| base64 -d > {_AUDIT_PATH}"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,

```python
def _install_kill_auditors(self):
    """SIGTERM/SIGINT → flush the trial audit, then honor the signal (IT-3)."""
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

            loop.add_signal_handler(sig, self._on_external_signal, sig.name, loop, previous)
```

            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.

                knobs,

            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)

                        # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                        # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                        # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:

                        # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                        # bounds the trial.
                        try:

        self, environment, knobs, ladder, outcome, deadline_epoch_ms=None,

```python
def _install_kill_auditors(self):
    """SIGTERM/SIGINT → flush the trial audit, then honor the signal (IT-3)."""
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    if threading.current_thread() is not threading.main_thread() or not hasattr(loop, "add_signal_handler"):
        return []
    installed = []
    for sig in _EXTERNAL_SIGNALS:
        try:
            previous = signal.getsignal(sig)
            loop.add_signal_handler(sig, self._on_external_signal, sig.name, loop, previous)
            installed.append((sig, previous))
        except (NotImplementedError, RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError):
            continue
    return installed

def _on_external_signal(self, signame, loop, previous):

    except RuntimeError:

        sig = getattr(signal, signame, None)
        if sig is not None:

            except Exception: pass
            os.kill(os.getpid(), sig)
```


{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                        loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
                    )
                    await self._maybe_checkpoint(environment, knobs, ladder)
                    if outcome:
                        # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                        # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                        # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                        # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed
                        # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                        # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                        # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:
                        # a SOLVED task scored 0). The bracket trick matches the
                        # agent process but not this command line, and any kill
                        # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                        # bounds the trial.
                        try:
                            await self.exec_as_root(
                                environment,
                                command="pkill -f '[f]a --session-root' || true",
                                timeout_sec=15,
                            )
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        try:
                            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=60)
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        if not exec_task.done():
                            exec_task.cancel()
                            # An abandoned cancelled task is GC-destroyed with
                            # "pending task" warnings and its exception never
                            # retrieved - await the cancellation instead. Only our
                            # own cancellation is swallowed; an external cancel of
                            # this coroutine still propagates.
                            try:
                                await exec_task
                            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                                if not exec_task.cancelled():
                                    raise
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        break
            # Natural completion: awaiting the task surfaces the exec's own
            # failure (e.g. NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) - today's semantics
            # verbatim. The audit records the true outcome class: a crash must
            # not be labelled "completed" (issue #1122 round 1).
            error = None
            if not outcome:
                try:
                    await exec_task
                except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised below
                    error = exc
            await self._write_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder,
                outcome or ("crashed" if error is not None else "completed"),
                deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
                cap=cap,
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # gh-1576 (I2): harbor's wait_for fired first — the incident's
            # exact kill class (run 38271607849: four trials killed at
            # 1800.000s, zero audit files). The container is still up
            # during teardown, so the flush lands. Never masked by an exec
            # failure; the cancellation always re-raises.
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        if outcome:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(
                f"fa agent killed by bench timeout ladder: {outcome}"
            )
        if error is not None:
            raise error

            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(

{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(

    """IT-1 (gh-1576 AC1/AC2): the external cap reaches the adapter's
    deadline and the audit — the incident fix, on the fake-harbor surface.
    """

    WATCH_ENV = {
        "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION": "1",
        "FA_STALL_GAP_SEC": "360",
        "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC": "3600",
    }

    def setUp(self):
        env = dict(self.WATCH_ENV)
        env.update(
            {
                "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC": "1800",
                "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG": json.dumps({"apiKeyEnvVar": "FA_KEY_FAKE"}),
                "FA_KEY_FAKE": "secret",

        return fa_agent_timeout.TimeoutKnobs.from_env()

        # AC1: external 1800s vs knob ceiling 3600s — the launch env that
        # reaches fa projects 1800 - 120 (wrap-up margin) = 1680s.
        agent = FakeAgent(launch_delay=0.05)

        after_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
        deadline = int(agent.launch_env["FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS"])

        self.assertLessEqual(deadline, after_ms + 1_681_000)

            )
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            task.cancel()
            with self.assertRaises(asyncio.CancelledError):

        self.assertEqual(payload["external_kill"]["cause"], "cancelled")

            int(agent.launch_env["FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS"]),
        )

        # same flush (previous=None in the test = no re-signal chain).
        agent = FakeAgent()

            task = asyncio.create_task(
                agent._run_with_deadline(self._knobs(), "task", object())
            )
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            agent._on_external_signal(

            )
            await asyncio.sleep(0.2)

            with self.assertRaises(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await task

        killed = [
            p
            for p in agent.audit_payloads
            if p.get("outcome") == "external_kill"
            and p.get("external_kill", {}).get("signal") == "SIGTERM"
        ]
        self.assertEqual(len(killed), 1, agent.audit_payloads)

        # IT-3/E3: the audit is written incrementally — a partial marker
        # exists from the first progress sample, before any kill.

{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                        loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
                    )
                    await self._maybe_checkpoint(environment, knobs, ladder)
                    if outcome:
                        # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                        # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                        # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                        # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed
                        # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                        # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                        # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:
                        # a SOLVED task scored 0). The bracket trick matches the
                        # agent process but not this command line, and any kill
                        # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                        # bounds the trial.
                        try:
                            await self.exec_as_root(
                                environment,
                                command="pkill -f '[f]a --session-root' || true",
                                timeout_sec=15,
                            )
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        try:
                            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=60)
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        if not exec_task.done():
                            exec_task.cancel()
                            # An abandoned cancelled task is GC-destroyed with
                            # "pending task" warnings and its exception never
                            # retrieved - await the cancellation instead. Only our
                            # own cancellation is swallowed; an external cancel of
                            # this coroutine still propagates.
                            try:
                                await exec_task
                            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                                if not exec_task.cancelled():
                                    raise
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        break
            # Natural completion: awaiting the task surfaces the exec's own
            # failure (e.g. NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) - today's semantics
            # verbatim. The audit records the true outcome class: a crash must
            # not be labelled "completed" (issue #1122 round 1).
            error = None
            if not outcome:
                try:
                    await exec_task
                except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised below
                    error = exc
            await self._write_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder,
                outcome or ("crashed" if error is not None else "completed"),
                deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
                cap=cap,
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # gh-1576 (I2): harbor's wait_for fired first — the incident's
            # exact kill class (run 38271607849: four trials killed at
            # 1800.000s, zero audit files). The container is still up
            # during teardown, so the flush lands. Never masked by an exec
            # failure; the cancellation always re-raises.
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        if outcome:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(
                f"fa agent killed by bench timeout ladder: {outcome}"
            )

{"newText":"    async def _write_audit(
        self, environment, knobs, ladder, outcome, deadline_epoch_ms=None,
        cap=None, checkpoint=False, external_kill=None,
    ) -> None:
        # AC4 (issue #1122): audit trail synced back with the agent logs.
        # AC6 (issue #1185): the audit also documents the harness-originated
        # share of the progress sample — the ⏳ liveness lines the pane
        # counter counts as progress. Both numbers are byte measures taken
        # where the file lives (one exec, no stream round-trip: a 600s+
        # trial can leave tens of MB of pane bytes, and a transport decode
        # would make len(utf-8) disagree with the ladder's live wc -c).
        # Fields drop when the stream is unreadable, never fabricated.
        # gh-1576: cap carries the cap-resolution block (winning source +
        # both inputs); checkpoint rows skip the stream measurement (they
        # are partial markers, written on the poll loop) and an
        # external_kill flush records which signal/cause ended the trial.
        if checkpoint:
            progress = liveness = None
        else:
            progress, liveness = await self._measure_streams(environment)
        record = _timeout.audit_dict(
            knobs,
            ladder if knobs is not None else None,
            outcome,
            progress_bytes=progress,
            liveness_bytes=liveness,
            deadline_epoch_ms=deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )
        if checkpoint:
            record["checkpoint"] = True
        if external_kill:
            record["external_kill"] = external_kill

                environment,

                    f"| base64 -d > {_AUDIT_PATH}"

{"newText":"class ExternalCapAdapterTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """IT-1 (gh-1576 AC1/AC2): the external cap reaches the adapter's
    deadline and the audit — the incident fix, on the fake-harbor surface.
    """

    WATCH_ENV = {
        "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION": "1",
        "FA_STALL_GAP_SEC": "360",
        "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC": "3600",
    }

    def setUp(self):
        env = dict(self.WATCH_ENV)
        env.update(
            {
                "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC": "1800",
                "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG": json.dumps({"apiKeyEnvVar": "FA_KEY_FAKE"}),
                "FA_KEY_FAKE": "secret",
            }
        )
        self._env = _clean_env(**env)
        self._env.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._env.stop)

    def _knobs(self):
        return fa_agent_timeout.TimeoutKnobs.from_env()

    def test_it1_deadline_is_external_cap_minus_margin(self):
        # AC1: external 1800s vs knob ceiling 3600s — the launch env that
        # reaches fa projects 1800 - 120 (wrap-up margin) = 1680s.
        agent = FakeAgent(launch_delay=0.05)
        before_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
        asyncio.run(agent._run_with_deadline(self._knobs(), "task", object()))
        after_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
        deadline = int(agent.launch_env["FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS"])
        self.assertGreaterEqual(deadline, before_ms + 1_679_000)
        self.assertLessEqual(deadline, after_ms + 1_681_000)

    def test_it1_audit_names_external_as_winning_source(self):
        # AC2: the audit record names the winning source and BOTH inputs.
        agent = FakeAgent(launch_delay=0.05)
        asyncio.run(agent._run_with_deadline(self._knobs(), "task", object()))
        payload = agent.audit_payload
        self.assertEqual(payload["outcome"], "completed")
        resolved = payload["cap_resolution"]
        self.assertEqual(resolved["winning_cap_source"], "external")
        self.assertEqual(resolved["external_cap_sec"], 1800.0)
        self.assertEqual(resolved["external_cap_status"], "known")
        self.assertEqual(resolved["knob_cap_sec"], 3600.0)
        self.assertEqual(resolved["effective_cap_sec"], 1800.0)
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["deadline_epoch_ms"],
            int(agent.launch_env["FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS"]),
        )

{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                        loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
                    )
                    await self._maybe_checkpoint(environment, knobs, ladder)
                    if outcome:
                        # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                        # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                        # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                        # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed
                        # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                        # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                        # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:
                        # a SOLVED task scored 0). The bracket trick matches the
                        # agent process but not this command line, and any kill
                        # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                        # bounds the trial.
                        try:
                            await self.exec_as_root(
                                environment,
                                command="pkill -f '[f]a --session-root' || true",
                                timeout_sec=15,
                            )
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        try:
                            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=60)
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        if not exec_task.done():
                            exec_task.cancel()
                            # An abandoned cancelled task is GC-destroyed with
                            # "pending task" warnings and its exception never
                            # retrieved - await the cancellation instead. Only our
                            # own cancellation is swallowed; an external cancel of
                            # this coroutine still propagates.
                            try:
                                await exec_task
                            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                                if not exec_task.cancelled():
                                    raise
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        break
            # Natural completion: awaiting the task surfaces the exec's own
            # failure (e.g. NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) - today's semantics
            # verbatim. The audit records the true outcome class: a crash must
            # not be labelled "completed" (issue #1122 round 1).
            error = None
            if not outcome:
                try:
                    await exec_task
                except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised below
                    error = exc
            await self._write_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder,
                outcome or ("crashed" if error is not None else "completed"),
                deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
                cap=cap,
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # gh-1576 (I2): harbor's wait_for fired first — the incident's
            # exact kill class (run 38271607849: four trials killed at
            # 1800.000s, zero audit files). The container is still up
            # during teardown, so the flush lands. Never masked by an exec
            # failure; the cancellation always re-raises.
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        if outcome:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(
                f"fa agent killed by bench timeout ladder: {outcome}"
            )
        if error is not None:
            raise error

{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                        loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
                    )
                    await self._maybe_checkpoint(environment, knobs, ladder)
                    if outcome:
                        # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                        # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                        # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                        # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed
                        # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                        # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                        # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:
                        # a SOLVED task scored 0). The bracket trick matches the
                        # agent process but not this command line, and any kill
                        # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                        # bounds the trial.
                        try:
                            await self.exec_as_root(
                                environment,
                                command="pkill -f '[f]a --session-root' || true",
                                timeout_sec=15,
                            )
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        try:
                            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=60)
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        if not exec_task.done():
                            exec_task.cancel()
                            # An abandoned cancelled task is GC-destroyed with
                            # "pending task" warnings and its exception never
                            # retrieved - await the cancellation instead. Only our
                            # own cancellation is swallowed; an external cancel of
                            # this coroutine still propagates.
                            try:
                                await exec_task
                            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                                if not exec_task.cancelled():
                                    raise
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        break
            # Natural completion: awaiting the task surfaces the exec's own
            # failure (e.g. NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) - today's semantics
            # verbatim. The audit records the true outcome class: a crash must
            # not be labelled "completed" (issue #1122 round 1).
            error = None
            if not outcome:
                try:
                    await exec_task
                except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised below
                    error = exc
            await self._write_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder,
                outcome or ("crashed" if error is not None else "completed"),
                deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
                cap=cap,
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # gh-1576 (I2): harbor's wait_for fired first — the incident's
            # exact kill class (run 38271607849: four trials killed at
            # 1800.000s, zero audit files). The container is still up
            # during teardown, so the flush lands. Never masked by an exec
            # failure; the cancellation always re-raises.
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        if outcome:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(
                f"fa agent killed by bench timeout ladder: {outcome}"
            )
        if error is not None:
            raise error

    async def _run_external_cap_only(self, instruction: str, environment) -> None:
        """Unsupervised exec under a known external cap (gh-1576).

        The harness owns the kill; the adapter's whole job here is I1+I2:
        fa sees the truthful deadline (via _provider_env) and every
        termination — clean exit, external cancellation, SIGTERM — leaves
        the audit record.
        """
        cap = self._cap
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                await self.exec_as_agent(
                    environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                    env=self._provider_env,
                )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, None, None, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        await self._write_audit(
            environment, None, None, "completed",
            deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )

        """Write the final external_kill audit once, then honor the signal.

{"newText":"    async def _write_audit(
        self, environment, knobs, ladder, outcome, deadline_epoch_ms=None,
        cap=None, checkpoint=False, external_kill=None,
    ) -> None:
        # AC4 (issue #1122): audit trail synced back with the agent logs.
        # AC6 (issue #1185): the audit also documents the harness-originated
        # share of the progress sample — the ⏳ liveness lines the pane
        # counter counts as progress. Both numbers are byte measures taken
        # where the file lives (one exec, no stream round-trip: a 600s+
        # trial can leave tens of MB of pane bytes, and a transport decode
        # would make len(utf-8) disagree with the ladder's live wc -c).
        # Fields drop when the stream is unreadable, never fabricated.
        # gh-1576: cap carries the cap-resolution block (winning source +
        # both inputs); checkpoint rows skip the stream measurement (they
        # are partial markers, written on the poll loop) and an
        # external_kill flush records which signal/cause ended the trial.
        if checkpoint:
            progress = liveness = None
        else:
            progress, liveness = await self._measure_streams(environment)
        record = _timeout.audit_dict(
            knobs,
            ladder if knobs is not None else None,
            outcome,
            progress_bytes=progress,
            liveness_bytes=liveness,
            deadline_epoch_ms=deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,
        )
        if checkpoint:
            record["checkpoint"] = True
        if external_kill:
            record["external_kill"] = external_kill
        payload = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(record).encode()).decode()
        try:
            await self.exec_as_agent(
                environment,
                command=(
                    f"mkdir -p /logs/agent && printf %s {payload} "
                    f"| base64 -d > {_AUDIT_PATH}"
                ),
                timeout_sec=15,
            )
        except Exception:
            pass","oldText":"    async def _write_audit(

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("test_fa_agent.py")

        self.knobs = knobs
        self.external_cap_sec = external_cap_sec""",
)

src = src.replace(
    """        if command.startswith("wc -c") or command.startswith("if p=$(wc -c"):
            value = self.counter["bytes"] if self.counter else 10
            return _ExecResult(f"{value} 0")""",
    """        if command.startswith("wc -c"):
            value = self.counter["bytes"] if self.counter else 10
            return _ExecResult(str(value))
        if command.startswith("if p=$(wc -c"):
            value = self.counter["bytes"] if self.counter else 10
            return _ExecResult(f"{value} 0")""",
)

# 3. malformed-cap test: poll fast so the completion window stays tight
src = src.replace(
    """        agent = FakeAgent(launch_delay=0.05)
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC": "soon"}):
            with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
                warnings.simplefilter("always")
                asyncio.run(
                    agent._run_with_deadline(self._knobs(), "task", object())
                )""",
    """        agent = FakeAgent(launch_delay=0.05)
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC": "soon"}):
            with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
                warnings.simplefilter("always")
                with mock.patch.object(fa_agent, "_POLL_SEC", 0.05):
                    asyncio.run(
                        agent._run_with_deadline(self._knobs(), "task", object())
                    )""",
)
p.write_text(src)
print("ok")
EOF"}

{"newText":"    def perform_task(
        self,
        instruction: str,
        session,
        logging_dir=None,
    ):
        session.copy_to_container(
            self._bundle_tarball,
            container_dir="/installed-agent",
        )
        knobs = _timeout.TimeoutKnobs.from_env()
        # gh-1576 cap resolution (I1), ONE resolution per trial: the
        # effective cap is min(external harness cap, adapter knobs) and
        # the launch line (via _run_agent_commands) exports the truthful
        # deadline in BOTH paths — with no cap input at all it is {}
        # (byte-identical: no export, fa never invents a clock).
        cap, deadline_ms = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline_ms
        self._deadline_env = (
            {"FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS": str(deadline_ms)}
            if deadline_ms is not None
            else {}
        )
        if knobs is None:
            # gh-1556 AC7: no adapter cap => no supervision (the stock
            # single exec; the harness's own kill still bounds the trial,
            # and a known external cap still arms fa's clock above).
            result = super().perform_task(instruction, session, logging_dir)
            # Issue #1123, corrected by gh-1209: fold fa's real session
            # usage into the result for ANY outcome where the agent process
            # actually ran — the timed-out trials are the expensive ones,
            # so skipping them reports zero spend on the costliest rows.
            # Only true never-started trials skip the fold: an installation
            # failure means fa never installed, and unknown_agent_error
            # means the harness never got the agent going. The fold itself
            # fails soft (zeros survive when no session file exists), so
            # folding a ran-but-empty trial is always safe.
            if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
                return result
            result = self._fold_session_usage(session, result, logging_dir)
            # gh-1576 (I2): with an external cap known, even this
            # unsupervised termination lands the audit — the failure mode
            # the harness recorded IS the outcome class.
            if cap is not None:
                self._write_audit(
                    logging_dir,
                    None,
                    None,
                    (
                        "completed"
                        if result.failure_mode in (None, FailureMode.NONE)
                        else str(result.failure_mode.value)
                    ),
                    deadline_epoch_ms=deadline_ms,
                    cap=cap,
                )
            return result
        # test_budget_sec stays 0: the agent phase does not consume the
        # verifier's budget — tb enforces the test phase separately, so
        # the abs ceiling is flat.
        return self._perform_task_with_deadline(
            knobs, instruction, session, logging_dir
        )","oldText":"    def perform_task(

- IT-4b: `_perform_task_with_deadline` writes audit with cap_resolution winning external + both inputs; checkpoints exist.

{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                        loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
                    )
                    await self._maybe_checkpoint(environment, knobs, ladder)
                    if outcome:
                        # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                        # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                        # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                        # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed
                        # its own shell (exit 143), the exception skipped the
                        # audit write AND the TimeoutError, and harbor recorded a
                        # ladder kill as an agent crash (TB 2.0 run 38150649548:
                        # a SOLVED task scored 0). The bracket trick matches the
                        # agent process but not this command line, and any kill
                        # failure is swallowed: harbor's own task timeout still
                        # bounds the trial.
                        try:
                            await self.exec_as_root(
                                environment,
                                command="pkill -f '[f]a --session-root' || true",
                                timeout_sec=15,
                            )
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        try:
                            await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=60)
                        except Exception:
                            pass
                        if not exec_task.done():
                            exec_task.cancel()
                            # An abandoned cancelled task is GC-destroyed with
                            # "pending task" warnings and its exception never
                            # retrieved - await the cancellation instead. Only our
                            # own cancellation is swallowed; an external cancel of
                            # this coroutine still propagates.
                            try:
                                await exec_task
                            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                                if not exec_task.cancelled():
                                    raise
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        break
            # Natural completion: awaiting the task surfaces the exec's own
            # failure (e.g. NonZeroAgentExitCodeError) - today's semantics
            # verbatim. The audit records the true outcome class: a crash must
            # not be labelled "completed" (issue #1122 round 1).
            error = None
            if not outcome:
                try:
                    await exec_task
                except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised below
                    error = exc
            await self._write_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder,
                outcome or ("crashed" if error is not None else "completed"),
                deadline_epoch_ms=self._deadline_epoch_ms,
                cap=cap,
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            # gh-1576 (I2): harbor's wait_for fired first — the incident's
            # exact kill class (run 38271607849: four trials killed at
            # 1800.000s, zero audit files). The container is still up
            # during teardown, so the flush lands. Never masked by an exec
            # failure; the cancellation always re-raises.
            await self._flush_external_kill_audit(
                environment, knobs, ladder, cap, cause="cancelled"
            )
            raise
        if outcome:
            raise asyncio.TimeoutError(
                f"fa agent killed by bench timeout ladder: {outcome}"
            )
        if error is not None:
            raise error

    async def _run_external_cap_only(self, instruction: str, environment) -> None:
        """Unsupervised exec under a known external cap (gh-1576).

        The harness owns the kill; the adapter's whole job here is I1+I2:
        fa sees the truthful deadline (via _provider_env) and every
        termination — clean exit, external cancellation, SIGTERM — leaves
        the audit record.
        """
        cap = self._cap
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                await self.exec_as_agent(
                    environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                    env=self._provider_env,
                )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:

{"newText":"    async def _write_audit(
        self, environment, knobs, ladder, outcome, deadline_epoch_ms=None,
        cap=None, checkpoint=False, external_kill=None,
    ) -> None:
        # AC4 (issue #1122): audit trail synced back with the agent logs.
        # AC6 (issue #1185): the audit also documents the harness-originated
        # share of the progress sample — the ⏳ liveness lines the pane
        # counter counts as progress. Both numbers are byte measures taken
        # where the file lives (one exec, no stream round-trip: a 600s+
        # trial can leave tens of MB of pane bytes, and a transport decode
        # would make len(utf-8) disagree with the ladder's live wc -c).
        # Fields drop when the stream is unreadable, never fabricated.
        # gh-1576: cap carries the cap-resolution block (winning source +
        # both inputs); checkpoint rows skip the stream measurement (they
        # are partial markers, written on the poll loop) and an
        # external_kill flush records which signal/cause ended the trial.
        if checkpoint:
            progress = liveness = None
        else:
            progress, liveness = await self._measure_streams(environment)
        record = _timeout.audit_dict(
            knobs,
            ladder if knobs is not None else None,
            outcome,
            progress_bytes=progress,
            liveness_bytes=liveness,
            deadline_epoch_ms=deadline_epoch_ms,
            cap=cap,

            record["checkpoint"] = True
        if external_kill:
            record["external_kill"] = external_kill

@unittest.skipUnless(TB_AVAILABLE, "terminal_bench not installed")
class TerminalBenchExternalCapTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """IT-4 (gh-1576): the same cap contract through the tb adapter.

    The tb harness cap (its --global-agent-timeout-sec / dataset caps) is
    normally the LARGER clock (bench.yml pins it above the adapter's own
    ceiling), so the external cap must be inert there (E4) — but when a
    harness ever caps BELOW the knobs (the harbor incident shape), the
    launch line, the audit, and the decider must all follow the smaller
    truth. Parity surface: identical audit schema to the harbor adapter.
    """

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmpdir.cleanup)
        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
            "legacy_fa_agent_extcap", root / "terminal_bench" / "fa_agent.py"
        )
        self.legacy_fa = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(self.legacy_fa)

    def _agent(self):
        tarball = Path(self.tmpdir.name) / "fa-bundle.tar.gz"
        tarball.write_bytes(b"")
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL": str(tarball)}):
            return self.legacy_fa.FaAgent()

    @staticmethod
    def _with_stock(agent, stock):
        return mock.patch.object(
            agent.legacy_fa.AbstractInstalledAgent if False else agent,
            "perform_task",
            side_effect=stock,
        )

    def _run_supervised(self, env_overrides, stock, logging_dir):
        agent = self._agent()
        session = FakeTmuxSession()
        env = clean_env_all(
            FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION="1",
            FA_STALL_GAP_SEC="360",
            FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="3600",
            FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG="{}",
            **env_overrides,
        )
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env), mock.patch.object(
            self.legacy_fa, "_POLL_SEC", 0.05
        ), mock.patch.object(
            self.legacy_fa.AbstractInstalledAgent, "perform_task",
            side_effect=stock,
        ):
            started = time.monotonic()
            agent.perform_task("instr", session, logging_dir)
        return agent, time.monotonic() - started

    def test_it4_launch_line_carries_the_external_cap_deadline(self):
        # AC1 parity: the launch line's FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS projects the
        # 1800s external cap - 120s margin, not the 3600s knob ceiling.
        logging_dir = Path(self.tmpdir.name)
        agent, _ = self._run_supervised(
            {fa_agent_timeout.EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV: "1800"},
            lambda **kwargs: "stock-result",
            logging_dir,
        )
        commands = agent._run_agent_commands("instr")
        self.assertEqual(len(commands), 1)
        self.assertIn("FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS=", commands[0].command)
        exported = int(
            commands[0].command.split("FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS=")[1].split(";")[0]
        )
        now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
        # 1680s ± the (sub-second) trial runtime.
        self.assertGreaterEqual(exported, now_ms + 1_679_000 - 5_000)
        self.assertLessEqual(exported, now_ms + 1_681_000)

    def test_it4_audit_names_the_winning_source(self):
        logging_dir = Path(self.tmpdir.name)
        self._run_supervised(
            {fa_agent_timeout.EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV: "1800"},
            lambda **kwargs: "stock-result",
            logging_dir,
        )
        audit = json.loads((logging_dir / "fa-agent-timeout.json").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(audit["outcome"], "completed")
        resolved = audit["cap_resolution"]
        self.assertEqual(resolved["winning_cap_source"], "external")
        self.assertEqual(resolved["external_cap_sec"], 1800.0)
        self.assertEqual(resolved["external_cap_status"], "known")
        self.assertEqual(resolved["knob_cap_sec"], 3600.0)
        self.assertEqual(resolved["effective_cap_sec"], 1800.0)

    def test_it4_larger_external_cap_is_inert(self):
        # E4 parity: bench.yml's shape — the tb harness cap sits ABOVE the
        # adapter ceiling, so nothing may change (byte-identical deadline).
        logging_dir = Path(self.tmpdir.name)
        agent, _ = self._run_supervised(
            {fa_agent_timeout.EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV: "86400"},
            lambda **kwargs: "stock-result",
            logging_dir,
        )
        audit = json.loads((logging_dir / "fa-agent-timeout.json").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(audit["cap_resolution"]["winning_cap_source"], "knobs")
        self.assertEqual(audit["cap_resolution"]["effective_cap_sec"], 3600.0)

    def test_it4_checkpoints_written_per_progress_sample(self):
        logging_dir = Path(self.tmpdir.name)

        def stock(**kwargs):
            for _ in range(6):
                time.sleep(0.05)
            return "stock-result"

        self._run_supervised(
            {fa_agent_timeout.EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV: "1800"},
            stock,
            logging_dir,
        )
        rows = [
            json.loads(line)
            for line in [  # one file, rewritten per write — read final only
                (logging_dir / "fa-agent-timeout.json").read_text()
            ]
        ]
        # The final row is the terminal audit; the checkpoint contract is
        # pinned on the harbor surface (same shared writer). Here we pin
        # that the terminal row carries the cap block and is not itself a
        # checkpoint.
        self.assertNotIn("checkpoint", rows[-1])

    def test_audit_schema_matches_the_harbor_surface(self):
        # IT-4 semantic-drift property: both adapters render the audit via
        # the SAME shared writer — the cap_resolution block and the
        # checkpoint/external_kill extras must be the identical schema.
        logging_dir = Path(self.tmpdir.name)
        self._run_supervised(
            {fa_agent_timeout.EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV: "1800"},
            lambda **kwargs: "stock-result",
            logging_dir,
        )
        tb_audit = json.loads((logging_dir / "fa-agent-timeout.json").read_text())
        env = clean_env_all(
            FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION="1",
            FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="3600",
            **{fa_agent_timeout.EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV: "1800"},
        )
        knobs = TimeoutKnobs.from_env(env)
        cap = fa_agent_timeout.resolve_cap(knobs, env)
        harbor_shaped = audit_dict(
            knobs, fa_agent_timeout.ProgressWatch(knobs), "completed",
            cap=cap, deadline_epoch_ms=42,
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            set(tb_audit["cap_resolution"]),
            set(harbor_shaped["cap_resolution"]),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            set(tb_audit) - {"deadline_sec", "extensions",
                             "last_progress_sec", "last_output_bytes"},
            set(harbor_shaped) - {"deadline_sec", "extensions",
                                  "last_progress_sec", "last_output_bytes"},
        )

    def test_external_cap_only_stock_run_exports_and_audits(self):
        # No adapter knobs, external cap known: the stock single-exec path
        # still arms fa's clock (I1) and lands the audit (I2).
        logging_dir = Path(self.tmpdir.name)
        agent = self._agent()
        session = FakeTmuxSession()
        sentinel = types.SimpleNamespace(
            failure_mode=self.legacy_fa.FailureMode.NONE
        )
        env = clean_env_all(
            FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG="{}",
            **{fa_agent_timeout.EXTERNAL_CAP_ENV: "1800"},
        )
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env), mock.patch.object(
            self.legacy_fa.AbstractInstalledAgent, "perform_task",
            side_effect=lambda *a, **k: sentinel,
        ) as stock:
            agent.perform_task("instr", session, logging_dir)
        stock.assert_called_once()
        commands = agent._run_agent_commands("instr")
        self.assertIn("FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS=", commands[0].command)
        audit = json.loads((logging_dir / "fa-agent-timeout.json").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(audit["outcome"], "completed")
        self.assertEqual(audit["policy"], "external-cap")
        self.assertNotIn("knobs", audit)
        self.assertEqual(audit["cap_resolution"]["winning_cap_source"], "external")

    def test_no_cap_no_knobs_stock_run_stays_byte_identical(self):
        # AC5/REG-2: no cap, no knobs — no export, no audit.
        logging_dir = Path(self.tmpdir.name)
        agent = self._agent()
        session = FakeTmuxSession()
        sentinel = types.SimpleNamespace(
            failure_mode=self.legacy_fa.FailureMode.NONE
        )
        with mock.patch.dict(
            os.environ, clean_env_all(FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG="{}")
        ), mock.patch.object(
            self.legacy_fa.AbstractInstalledAgent, "perform_task",
            side_effect=lambda *a, **k: sentinel,
        ):
            agent.perform_task("instr", session, logging_dir)
        commands = agent._run_agent_commands("instr")
        self.assertNotIn("FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS", commands[0].command)
        self.assertFalse((logging_dir / "fa-agent-timeout.json").exists())

{"newText":"    async def _run_with_deadline(
        self, knobs: "_timeout.TimeoutKnobs", instruction: str, environment
    ) -> None:
        """Supervise the fa exec under the issue #1122 ladder.

        Progress = growth of /logs/agent/fa.txt (the tee'd agent output the
        command already writes). On stall/hard-ceiling: pkill fa, then raise
        asyncio.TimeoutError — inside harbor's own wait_for this is
        indistinguishable from the harness's native timeout, so the trial
        classifies as AgentTimeoutError exactly as today. Natural
        completion (including a non-zero fa exit) re-raises whatever the
        exec raised, byte-for-byte today's semantics.

        gh-1576: the kill deadlines clamp to the external harness cap (the
        decider dies at min(knob deadline, external) and names the winner
        external_cap), the audit is checkpointed incrementally so even a
        SIGKILL leaves the last progress sample, and BOTH external kill
        paths — a cancellation of this coroutine (harbor's own wait_for
        firing first) and a SIGTERM/SIGINT to this process — flush a final
        outcome=external_kill record (I2). The incremental checkpoints are
        what survives a SIGKILL; nothing else can (non-goal E3).
        """
        cap, deadline = _timeout.resolve_deadline(knobs)
        self._cap = cap
        self._deadline_epoch_ms = deadline
        ladder = (
            # gh-1556 (Class C): parity with bench/terminal_bench/
            # fa_agent.py — when a watch knob is set the kill decision is
            # the gap-aware ProgressWatch (issue #1392/#1430), not the
            # retired byte-growth ladder. bench-harbor.yml now sets the
            # knobs on every shard, so watch mode is the bench default;
            # with knobs removed the legacy ProgressLadder runs
            # byte-for-byte (round-2 REG). gh-1576: both deciders clamp
            # their kill deadline to the external cap when one is known.
            _timeout.ProgressWatch(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
            if knobs.progress_watch
            else _timeout.ProgressLadder(
                knobs,
                external_cap_sec=cap.external_cap_sec if cap else None,
            )
        )
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        start = loop.time()
        outcome = None
        self._audit_terminal = False
        self._checkpoint_state = None
        exec_task = asyncio.create_task(
            self.exec_as_agent(
                environment, command=self._agent_command(instruction),
                env=self._provider_env,
            )
        )
        try:
            with self._kill_auditors():
                while not exec_task.done():
                    remaining = ladder.kill_at - (loop.time() - start)
                    await asyncio.sleep(min(_POLL_SEC, max(remaining, 0.05)))
                    outcome = ladder.evaluate(
                        loop.time() - start, await self._progress_bytes(environment)
                    )
                    await self._maybe_checkpoint(environment, knobs, ladder)
                    if outcome:
                        # gh-1556 AC1: the kill is best-effort and can never
                        # replace the ladder's TimeoutError. The pre-fix command
                        # was `pkill -f 'fa --session-root'` — the exec wrapper's
                        # OWN cmdline contains that pattern, so pkill SIGTERMed

        self, environment, knobs, ladder, outcome, deadline_epoch_ms=None,
        cap=None, checkpoint=False, external_kill=None,

        # AC4 (issue #1122): audit trail synced back with the agent logs.

        # share of the progress sample — the ⏳ liveness lines the pane
        # counter counts as progress. Both numbers are byte measures taken

        # trial can leave tens of MB of pane bytes, and a transport decode
